结果将在国际出版物和会议演示文稿中以及以通俗易懂的语言摘要的形式传播给参与的患者。 [10.1136/bmjopen-2026-119939]
185名RSV感染儿童中,中位年龄为2个月,其中51.9%为男性。住院时间较长(>2天)的患者入住PICU、无创通气、机械通气和继发细菌感染的比例较高。实验室检查结果显示,长期住院组的淋巴细胞计数和 BUN 水平较高,而 MPV 水平较低。没有发生 死亡率。 [10.4274/forbes.galenos.2026.57704]
由于 RIG-I 水平较低,RSV 非结构蛋白 2 使婴​​儿 BEpiC 中的 RIG-I-STAT3 信号失活,而成人 BEpiC 则保持强大的 RIG-I 信号并抵抗失活,小鼠的急性病毒感染会触发 BEpiC 中持续的表观遗传和转录组变化,类似于人类年龄相关状态。 [10.1038/s41467-026-75842-8]

papers.title: Palivizumab for respiratory syncytial virus immunoprophylaxis in high-risk populations in Qatar: a call for action
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Preterm and high-risk infants are at increased risk of severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection, leading to prolonged hospitalization, intensive care unit admissions, respiratory support and death. Although, RSV prevention is a major health priority in Qatar, national guidelines for RSV prophylaxis are currently lacking. AREAS COVERED: This expert opinion summarizes the burden of RSV in Qatar and the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) along with current immunoprophylaxis practices and real-world evidence on the effectiveness of palivizumab in high-risk infants. Evidence from a literature review was supplemented by expert insights relevant to Qatar and the GCC to address data gaps and heterogeneity in RSV prophylaxis. The integrated findings support context-specific recommendations. EXPERT OPINION: A steering committee with 16 experts was convened in December 2024 to review the available evidence and discuss challenges in RSV prevention among high-risk infants in Qatar. The experts reviewed the literature and reached consensus for the recommendations. This paper provides a localized, evidence-based action plan for the healthcare community, while facilitating optimal utilization of resources and cost-effective practices for RSV prophylaxis in Qatar. It also acknowledges the necessity to collaborate with other GCC countries and develop a regional protocol to further strengthen the RSV prevention efforts.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) immunoprophylaxis in high-risk infants in Qatar, focusing on the pathogen RSV, the disease burden in preterm and high-risk populations, and the intervention palivizumab. The central question addresses the burden of RSV, current immunoprophylaxis practices, and the effectiveness of palivizumab in this specific high-risk population.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is an expert opinion summarizing RSV burden and immunoprophylaxis practices in Qatar and the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC), supplemented by expert insights to address data gaps and heterogeneity. It includes a steering committee of 16 experts who reviewed literature and reached consensus for localized recommendations.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that preterm and high-risk infants face severe RSV infection risks, including prolonged hospitalization, ICU admissions, respiratory support, and death. It supports context-specific recommendations for RSV prophylaxis in Qatar, emphasizing the need for localized, evidence-based action plans and resource optimization.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review acknowledges heterogeneity in RSV prophylaxis practices and data gaps in Qatar and the GCC. It highlights the lack of national guidelines for RSV prophylaxis in Qatar as a critical unresolved issue.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review calls for collaboration with other GCC countries to develop a regional protocol for RSV prevention. It emphasizes the necessity of strengthening RSV prevention efforts through coordinated, context-specific strategies and resource utilization in Qatar.

analysis.summary_en: This expert review focuses on respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) immunoprophylaxis in high-risk infants in Qatar, addressing the pathogen's burden, current practices, and the effectiveness of palivizumab. It highlights severe outcomes in preterm and high-risk infants, including prolonged hospitalization and ICU admissions. The review synthesizes literature and expert insights to propose localized, evidence-based recommendations for RSV prophylaxis in Qatar, where national guidelines are currently lacking. Key gaps include heterogeneity in practices and data limitations, necessitating regional collaboration to develop standardized protocols. The authors advocate for optimized resource utilization and a coordinated approach to strengthen RSV prevention efforts across the Gulf Cooperation Council.

elements_en.scope_and_question: The review examines respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) immunoprophylaxis in high-risk infants in Qatar, focusing on the pathogen RSV, the disease burden in preterm and high-risk populations, and the intervention palivizumab. elements_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that preterm and high-risk infants face severe RSV infection risks, including prolonged hospitalization, ICU admissions, respiratory support, and death. elements_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review acknowledges heterogeneity in RSV prophylaxis practices and data gaps in Qatar and the GCC. It highlights the lack of national guidelines for RSV prophylaxis in Qatar as a critical unresolved issue.
elements_en.research_and_practice_implications: The review calls for collaboration with other GCC countries to develop a regional protocol for RSV prevention. It emphasizes the necessity of strengthening RSV prevention efforts through coordinated, context-specific strategies and resource utilization in Qatar.

papers.title_zh: 帕利珠单抗用于卡塔尔高危人群的 呼吸道合胞病毒 免疫预防:呼吁采取行动
papers.source_body_en: INTRODUCTION: Preterm and high-risk infants are at increased risk of severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection, leading to prolonged hospitalization, intensive care unit admissions, respiratory support and death. Although, RSV prevention is a major health priority in Qatar, national guidelines for RSV prophylaxis are currently lacking. AREAS COVERED: This expert opinion summarizes the burden of RSV in Qatar and the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) along with current immunoprophylaxis practices and real-world evidence on the effectiveness of palivizumab in high-risk infants. Evidence from a literature review was supplemented by expert insights relevant to Qatar and the GCC to address data gaps and heterogeneity in RSV prophylaxis. The integrated findings support context-specific recommendations. EXPERT OPINION: A steering committee with 16 experts was convened in December 2024 to review the available evidence and discuss challenges in RSV prevention among high-risk infants in Qatar. The experts reviewed the literature and reached consensus for the recommendations. This paper provides a localized, evidence-based action plan for the healthcare community, while facilitating optimal utilization of resources and cost-effective practices for RSV prophylaxis in Qatar. It also acknowledges the necessity to collaborate with other GCC countries and develop a regional protocol to further strengthen the RSV prevention efforts.

papers.title: Respiratory syncytial virus infection in COPD exacerbations: the RECODE study protocol.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) often suffer episodes of exacerbation (ECOPD). Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is an increasingly recognised cause of illness in adults. Yet the prevalence of RSV during ECOPD and its association with clinically relevant outcomes remain insufficiently defined. The RECODE study sought to determine the prevalence of RSV infection in patients with ECOPD and to assess the association between RSV and hospitalisation, length of stay, acute cardiovascular events and/or death. METHODS AND ANALYSIS: Prospective, multicentre, observational, controlled (RSV-positive cases vs RSV-negative controls), longitudinal study (NCT06735612). Adults ≥50 years with ECOPD will be enrolled at urgent-care presentation (V1), contacted by telephone at day 15 (V2) and seen in the clinic at 3 months (V3). RSV status will be determined by Reverse Transcription (RT-PCR) on nasopharyngeal swabs; additional measures include paired serology, routine clinical data, spirometry at V3 and predefined outcomes. ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: The leading Ethics Committee was that of Clinic Barcelona (HCB/2024/0771). All participating centres accepted this approval or requested local approval from their respective Institutional Review Boards (Appendix). Results will be disseminated in international publications and meeting presentations as well as in a plain language summary to be distributed among participating patients. TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT06735612.

papers.title: Maternal Immunization Against Respiratory Syncytial Virus: An Integrative Review of Efficacy, Safety, and Implementation
papers.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of severe lower respiratory tract infection in young infants and accounts for substantial morbidity, hospitalization, and mortality worldwide, with the highest burden concentrated in the first months of life, when immunological and anatomical immaturity favors severe disease. Maternal vaccination has emerged as a strategy to bridge this window of vulnerability through the transplacental transfer of neutralizing antibodies. This integrative review synthesizes scientific articles published between 2022 and 2026, including systematic reviews, meta-analyses, narrative reviews, and position statements from national and international scientific societies, addressing the epidemiology, clinical manifestations, diagnosis, mechanism of action, efficacy, safety, and public health impact of maternal RSV immunization. The bivalent prefusion F protein vaccine (RSVpreF; Abrysvo®), administered as a single intramuscular dose between 32 and 36 weeks of gestation, induces maternal IgG that is transferred to the fetus and confers passive protection during the first six months of life. In the phase 3 MATISSE trial, vaccination demonstrated 81.8% efficacy against severe RSV lower respiratory tract infection within 90 days of birth and 69.4% within 180 days, alongside reductions in hospitalization. The safety profile was favorable, with predominantly mild and transient adverse events; a numerical imbalance in preterm birth remains under surveillance and underlies the precautionary gestational window. Maternal vaccination and long-acting monoclonal antibodies (nirsevimab) are best regarded as complementary rather than competing strategies. Current evidence supports maternal immunization as one of the most effective measures to reduce the burden of RSV disease in early infancy.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) as the pathogen, focusing on maternal immunization to protect infants under six months of age, a population with high vulnerability due to immunological and anatomical immaturity. The central question addresses the efficacy, safety, and implementation of maternal RSV vaccination, including the role of transplacental antibody transfer and complementary interventions.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This integrative review synthesizes articles published between 2022 and 2026, including systematic reviews, meta-analyses, narrative reviews, and position statements from national and international scientific societies. The review method involves synthesizing diverse evidence types without explicit pooled estimates or meta-analytic procedures.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The bivalent prefusion F protein vaccine (RSVpreF; Abrysvo®), administered as a single intramuscular dose between 32 and 36 weeks of gestation, induces maternal IgG that is transferred to the fetus and confers passive protection during the first six months of life. In the phase 3 MATISSE trial, vaccination demonstrated 81.8% efficacy against severe RSV lower respiratory tract infection within 90 days of birth and 69.4% within 180 days, alongside reductions in hospitalization. Current evidence supports maternal immunization as one of the most effective measures to reduce the burden of RSV disease in early infancy.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: A numerical imbalance in preterm birth remains under surveillance and underlies the precautionary gestational window of 32 to 36 weeks. The review does not report long-term safety outcomes beyond the initial surveillance period or data on populations excluded from trials, such as immunocompromised pregnant individuals.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review highlights the need for ongoing surveillance of preterm birth outcomes following maternal RSV vaccination. It also emphasizes the complementary role of maternal vaccination and long-acting monoclonal antibodies (nirsevimab) rather than viewing them as competing strategies, suggesting integrated implementation strategies.

analysis.summary_en: This integrative review evaluates maternal immunization against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) to protect infants under six months of age, a population at high risk due to immunological immaturity. The review synthesizes evidence from 2022 to 2026, including systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and position statements, focusing on efficacy, safety, and implementation. Key findings include the high efficacy of the bivalent prefusion F protein vaccine (RSVpreF; Abrysvo®) in reducing severe RSV infections and hospitalizations in infants, with efficacy of 81.8% within 90 days and 69.4% within 180 days post-birth. The review supports maternal immunization as an effective strategy but notes a precautionary gestational window due to a numerical imbalance in preterm births under surveillance. It also underscores the complementary nature of maternal vaccination and monoclonal antibodies (nirsevimab) for optimal infant protection.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述将 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 视为病原体,重点关注孕产妇免疫接种,以保护六个月以下的婴儿,该人群由于免疫和解剖学不成熟而易受感染。核心问题涉及母体 RSV 疫苗接种 的有效性、安全性和实施,包括经胎盘抗体转移和补充干预措施的作用。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 这篇综合综述综合了 2022 年至 2026 年发表的文章,包括系统综述、荟萃分析、叙述性综述以及来自国家和国际科学协会的立场声明。审查方法涉及综合不同的证据类型,而无需明确的汇总估计或荟萃分析程序。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 二价预融合 F 蛋白 疫苗(RSVpreF;Abrysvo®)在妊娠 32 至 36 周期间以单次肌肉注射剂量给药,可诱导母体 IgG 转移至胎儿,并在生命的前六个月内提供被动保护。在 MATISSE 3 期试验中,疫苗接种 在出生 90 天内对严重 RSV 下呼吸道感染的疗效为 81.8%,在 180 天内对严重 RSV 下呼吸道感染的疗效为 69.4%,同时减少了住院治疗。目前的证据支持孕产妇免疫接种是减轻婴儿早期 RSV 疾病负担的最有效措施之一。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 监测 下的早产数量不平衡仍然存在,并且是 32 至 36 周的预防性妊娠窗口的基础。该综述不报告初始 监测 期之后的长期安全结果或被排除在试验之外的人群(例如免疫功能低下的怀孕个体)的数据。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该审查强调了在母亲 RSV 疫苗接种 后持续进行 监测 早产结局的必要性。它还强调母体疫苗接种和长效单克隆抗体(尼塞韦单抗)的互补作用,而不是将它们视为竞争策略,建议综合实施策略。

papers.title: Modulation of Respiratory Diseases by the Endocannabinoid System: A Therapeutic Perspective.
papers.abstract: Respiratory system diseases represent a major global health burden, characterized by high prevalence and significant morbidity and mortality. The respiratory tract's direct and continuous exposure to the external environment makes it particularly vulnerable to pathogens, pollutants and other injurious agents. This exposure often triggers excessive inflammatory responses and compromises the integrity of the air-blood barrier, leading to impaired gas exchange, hypoxia and respiratory failure. Therefore, modulating pulmonary inflammation and enhancing barrier function are critical therapeutic objectives. The endocannabinoid system, a ubiquitous signalling network comprising cannabinoid receptors, endogenous ligands and metabolic enzymes, has emerged as a crucial modulator of these processes. This review summarizes the role of the ECS in major respiratory diseases, including asthma, pulmonary fibrosis, respiratory syncytial virus infection and acute lung injury. The evidence highlights the therapeutic potential of targeting the ECS through strategies such as receptor-specific ligands and inhibitors of endocannabinoid-degrading enzymes. However, the context-dependent nature of ECS modulation necessitates precise intervention. Future efforts should focus on developing selective therapeutics and validating their efficacy in clinical settings, positioning the ECS as a sophisticated target for innovative respiratory disease management.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines the role of the endocannabinoid system (ECS) in modulating respiratory diseases, focusing on its therapeutic potential for conditions such as asthma, pulmonary fibrosis, respiratory syncytial virus infection, and acute lung injury. The central question addresses how ECS modulation—via receptor-specific ligands or inhibitors of endocannabinoid-degrading enzymes—could mitigate excessive pulmonary inflammation and restore air-blood barrier integrity to improve gas exchange and reduce respiratory failure.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This is a narrative review summarizing the ECS's involvement in respiratory diseases without explicit systematic search methods, eligibility criteria, or study counts. The review synthesizes evidence on ECS modulation strategies but does not report databases searched, search dates, or a meta-analysis process.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that the ECS is a critical modulator of pulmonary inflammation and barrier function, with therapeutic potential in respiratory diseases. It highlights the need for precise ECS-targeted interventions due to the system's context-dependent effects, emphasizing receptor-specific ligands and enzyme inhibitors as promising strategies.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review identifies the context-dependent nature of ECS modulation as a key unresolved issue, complicating the development of universally effective therapeutics. It also notes the lack of clinical validation for ECS-targeted strategies in respiratory diseases, leaving mechanisms and efficacy in human populations insufficiently characterized.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review prioritizes the development of selective ECS therapeutics and their validation in clinical settings to establish efficacy and safety. It also calls for mechanistic studies to clarify the context-dependent effects of ECS modulation in respiratory diseases, ensuring targeted and effective interventions.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述探讨了内源性大麻素系统 (ECS) 在调节呼吸系统疾病中的作用,重点关注其对哮喘、肺纤维化、呼吸道合胞病毒 感染和急性肺损伤等疾病的治疗潜力。核心问题涉及 ECS 调节(通过受体特异性配体或内源性大麻素降解酶抑制剂)如何减轻过度的肺部炎症并恢复气血屏障的完整性,从而改善气体交换并减少呼吸衰竭。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 这是一篇叙述性综述,总结了 ECS 在呼吸系统疾病方面的参与,没有明确的系统搜索方法、资格标准或研究计数。该综述综合了 ECS 调制策略的证据,但没有报告搜索的数据库、搜索日期或荟萃分析过程。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该综述的结论是,ECS 是肺部炎症和屏障功能的关键调节剂,具有治疗呼吸系统疾病的潜力。它强调了由于系统的上下文相关效应而需要精确的 ECS 靶向干预措施,并强调受体特异性配体和酶抑制剂是有前途的策略。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述将 ECS 调节的背景依赖性确定为一个未解决的关键问题,使普遍有效的治疗方法的开发变得复杂化。它还指出,针对呼吸系统疾病的 ECS 靶向策略缺乏临床验证,导致对人群的机制和疗效描述不充分。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该审查优先考虑选择性 ECS 疗法的开发及其在临床环境中的验证,以确定疗效和安全性。它还呼吁进行机制研究,以阐明 ECS 调节对呼吸系统疾病的背景依赖性影响,确保有针对性和有效的干预措施。

papers.abstract_zh: 呼吸系统疾病是全球主要的健康负担,其特点是高 患病率 和显着的发病率和 死亡率。呼吸道直接且持续地暴露于外部环境,使其特别容易受到病原体、污染物和其他有害物质的侵害。这种暴露通常会引发过度的炎症反应,损害气血屏障的完整性,导致气体交换受损、缺氧和呼吸衰竭。因此,调节肺部炎症和增强屏障功能是关键的治疗目标。内源性大麻素系统是一种普遍存在的信号网络,由大麻素受体、内源性配体和代谢酶组成,已成为这些过程的关键调节剂。本综述总结了 ECS 在主要呼吸系统疾病中的作用,包括哮喘、肺纤维化、呼吸道合胞病毒 感染和急性肺损伤。证据强调了通过受体特异性配体和内源性大麻素降解酶抑制剂等策略靶向 ECS 的治疗潜力。然而,ECS 调制的上下文相关性质需要精确的干预。未来的努力应集中于开发选择性疗法并在临床环境中验证其疗效,将 ECS 定位为创新呼吸系统疾病管理的复杂目标。

papers.title: Screening and mechanism analysis of core target genes for resveratrol inhibiting respiratory syncytial virus.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), a single-stranded negative-sense RNA virus, is a major pathogen of acute respiratory tract infections, posing severe threats to the health of infants, the elderly and immunocompromised individuals. While approved vaccines for older adults and monoclonal antibody prophylaxis for infants are available, effective therapeutic drugs remain scarce. Resveratrol, a phenolic compound naturally present in grapes, berries and other foods, has been confirmed to exhibit anti-RSV activity, but its molecular mechanism of action remains unclear. analysis.research_question_and_background: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) causes severe acute respiratory infections in vulnerable populations, and despite available vaccines and prophylaxis, effective therapeutic drugs remain limited. The study was needed to clarify the molecular mechanism by which resveratrol, a natural phenolic compound with reported anti-RSV activity, exerts its effects.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This in-silico study screened core target genes and signaling pathways of resveratrol against RSV using computational biology approaches. It integrated 261 resveratrol-related targets and 1196 RSV-related targets from public databases to identify overlapping targets and perform network and pathway analyses.
analysis.methods: Overlapping targets were identified using Venny 2.1.0, followed by protein-protein interaction network construction via STRING/Cytoscape and topological analysis to screen core targets. GO and KEGG enrichment analyses were performed using the DAVID database, and molecular docking validation was conducted with PyMOL/AutoDock to assess binding stability.
analysis.main_results: Ten core targets including EGFR, SRC, HSP90AA1 and ALB were identified. GO enrichment highlighted biological processes such as PI3K-Akt signal transduction and MAPK cascade regulation, while KEGG pathways were enriched in the Ras signaling pathway and others. Molecular docking showed stable binding of resveratrol to core targets, with all binding energies below -5 kcal/mol.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study interprets that resveratrol may inhibit RSV by targeting host proteins such as EGFR and SRC and modulating key pathways including PI3K-Akt and Ras, complementing existing evidence of its direct interaction with viral proteins. It provides novel insights for anti-RSV drug development and a theoretical foundation for experimental validation.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest potential host-targeted therapeutic strategies for RSV using resveratrol, offering a mechanistic basis for future antiviral drug development and experimental studies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: As an in-silico study, the evidence is limited by the lack of in vitro or in vivo validation, which constrains the strength of causal inference and generalizability. The confidence in the findings is therefore assessed as moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This in-silico study investigated the molecular mechanism by which resveratrol may inhibit respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) by screening core target genes and signaling pathways. Using computational biology approaches, the authors integrated 261 resveratrol-related and 1196 RSV-related targets to identify 67 overlapping targets, which were analyzed via protein-protein interaction networks and topological screening to yield ten core targets including EGFR, SRC, HSP90AA1 and ALB. GO enrichment highlighted biological processes such as PI3K-Akt signal transduction and MAPK cascade regulation, while KEGG pathway analysis enriched the Ras signaling pathway. Molecular docking confirmed stable binding of resveratrol to core targets, with all binding energies below -5 kcal/mol. The study interprets that resveratrol may exert anti-RSV effects by targeting host proteins and modulating key pathways, complementing evidence of its direct interaction with viral proteins. While the findings provide novel insights and a theoretical foundation for anti-RSV drug development, the lack of in vitro or in vivo validation limits causal inference and generalizability, resulting in a moderate confidence assessment.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 在易感人群中引起严重的急性呼吸道感染,尽管有可用的 疫苗 和预防措施,但有效的治疗药物仍然有限。这项研究需要阐明白藜芦醇(一种据报道具有抗 RSV 活性的天然酚类化合物)发挥作用的分子机制。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项计算机研究利用计算生物学方法筛选了白藜芦醇对抗 RSV 的核心靶基因和信号通路。它整合了公共数据库中的 261 个白藜芦醇相关目标和 1196 个 RSV 相关目标,以识别重叠目标并进行网络和路径分析。
elements_zh.methods: 使用Venny 2.1.0识别重叠靶标,然后通过STRING/Cytoscape构建蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用网络并进行拓扑分析以筛选核心靶标。使用DAVID数据库进行GO和KEGG富集分析,并使用PyMOL/AutoDock进行分子对接验证以评估结合稳定性。
elements_zh.main_results: 确定了 EGFR、SRC、HSP90AA1 和 ALB 等 10 个核心靶点。GO 富集突出了 PI3K-Akt 信号转导和 MAPK 级联调控等生物过程,而 KEGG 通路则富集了 Ras 信号通路等。分子对接显示白藜芦醇与核心靶点稳定结合,所有结合能均低于-5 kcal/mol。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究解释说,白藜芦醇可能通过靶向 宿主 蛋白(例如 EGFR 和 SRC)并调节包括 PI3K-Akt 和 Ras 在内的关键通路来抑制 RSV,补充了其与病毒蛋白直接相互作用的现有证据。它为抗 RSV 药物开发提供了新颖的见解,并为实验验证提供了理论基础。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,使用白藜芦醇针对 RSV 具有潜在的 宿主 靶向治疗策略,为未来的 宿主 药物开发和实验研究提供了机制基础。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 作为一项计算机研究,证据因缺乏体外或体内验证而受到限制,这限制了因果推理和普遍性的强度。因此,研究结果的可信度被评估为中等。

analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究解释说,白藜芦醇可能通过靶向 宿主 蛋白(例如 EGFR 和 SRC)并调节包括 PI3K-Akt 和 Ras 在内的关键通路来抑制 RSV,补充了其与病毒蛋白直接相互作用的现有证据。它为抗 RSV 药物开发提供了新颖的见解,并为实验验证提供了理论基础。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,使用白藜芦醇针对 RSV 具有潜在的 宿主 靶向治疗策略,为未来的 宿主 药物开发和实验研究提供了机制基础。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 作为一项计算机研究,证据因缺乏体外或体内验证而受到限制,这限制了因果推理和普遍性的强度。因此,研究结果的可信度被评估为中等。

papers.title: Infant respiratory syncytial virus and childhood asthma: a nationwide registry-based, sibling-controlled, and genome-wide association study
papers.abstract: BackgroundEarly-life respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection is associated with childhood recurrent wheeze or asthma (RW/A), but causality and shared genetic liability remain unclear. MethodsWe combined Finnish nationwide registries and Nordic genetic cohorts. First, in 965 312 Finnish children born between 1998 and 2014, we defined severe RSV as RSV hospitalisation before age 1 year, and recurrent wheezing or asthma (RW/A) as inhaled medication reimbursement between ages 1 and 7 years, and compared medication and eosinophil trajectories by RSV history. Second, we assessed familial confounding in 527 776 full siblings and 15 667 RW/A- discordant pairs. Third, we performed a genome-wide association study (GWAS) of RSV susceptibility with meta-analysis across six Nordic cohorts (3 107 cases, 92 091 controls) and two-sample Mendelian randomisation (2SMR) using 155 asthma-associated variants. FindingsRSV-associated RW/A showed higher inhaled medication use at ages 1-2 years but lower use after age 5, and lower mean blood eosinophils (0{middle dot}341 vs 0{middle dot}398x10{square}/L; p=0{middle dot}008) than RW/A without RSV hospitalisation. In RW/A-discordant sibling pairs, RSV hospitalisation was associated with RW/A (OR 2{middle dot}8; 95% CI 2{middle dot}4-3{middle dot}2), while unaffected siblings also had elevated RW/A prevalence. GWAS identified an RSV association at APBB1IP (rs787036; {beta}=0{middle dot}209; p=8{middle dot}80x10-{square}). 2SMR provided no evidence that asthma genetic liability influenced RSV susceptibility. InterpretationThe RSV-asthma association is unlikely to be explained by shared genetic or environmental factors, and RSV-associated RW/A shows a distinct trajectory. These findings help prioritise long-term outcomes for RSV prevention trials and monitoring. FundingPaivikki and Sakari Sohlberg Foundation, Foundation for Pediatric Research, Sigrid Juselius Foundation, Orion Research Foundation, the Research Council of Norway.

papers.title_original: Infant respiratory syncytial virus and childhood asthma: a nationwide registry-based, sibling-controlled, and genome-wide association study

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines whether early-life respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection causes childhood recurrent wheeze or asthma (RW/A), focusing on causality, shared genetic liability, and distinct clinical trajectories. The central question addresses the association between severe RSV infection (hospitalisation before age 1 year) and RW/A (medication reimbursement between ages 1 and 7 years) in a nationwide registry-based cohort.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review synthesizes evidence from a nationwide registry-based study in Finland (1998–2014) combining registry data with Nordic genetic cohorts. It includes a genome-wide association study (GWAS) across six Nordic cohorts (3,107 cases, 92,091 controls) and two-sample Mendelian randomisation (2SMR) using 155 asthma-associated variants. The review does not explicitly report eligibility criteria, search dates, or databases beyond the described cohorts.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that RSV-associated RW/A exhibits distinct clinical features, including higher inhaled medication use at ages 1–2 years but lower use after age 5, and lower mean blood eosinophils (0.341 vs 0.398 x109/L; p=0.008) compared to RW/A without RSV hospitalisation. Sibling-controlled analyses show an association between RSV hospitalisation and RW/A (OR 2.8; 95% CI 2.4–3.2), though unaffected siblings also had elevated RW/A prevalence. GWAS identified an RSV association at APBB1IP (rs787036; β=0.209; p=8.80x10−8), and 2SMR found no evidence that asthma genetic liability influences RSV susceptibility.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights unresolved questions about the causal pathway between RSV and RW/A, as sibling analyses suggest potential unmeasured confounding despite familial controls. The distinct eosinophil trajectory in RSV-associated RW/A remains mechanistically unexplained, and the GWAS signal at APBB1IP requires further validation and functional studies to clarify its role in RSV susceptibility.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review prioritises long-term outcome monitoring in RSV prevention trials to assess whether reducing severe RSV infections mitigates RW/A risk. It also calls for mechanistic studies to elucidate the eosinophil trajectory differences and functional validation of the APBB1IP locus to determine its biological relevance to RSV susceptibility.

analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates the association between early-life severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection and childhood recurrent wheeze or asthma (RW/A) using nationwide registry data, sibling-controlled analyses, and genetic studies. Key findings include distinct clinical trajectories in RSV-associated RW/A, such as higher early medication use but lower eosinophil levels, and an association with RW/A in sibling analyses (OR 2.8). A genome-wide association study identified a potential RSV susceptibility locus (APBB1IP), while Mendelian randomisation found no shared genetic liability between asthma and RSV. Unresolved questions include the causal pathway, confounding in sibling analyses, and the mechanistic basis of eosinophil differences. The review prioritises long-term monitoring in RSV prevention trials and mechanistic studies to validate genetic findings and clarify causality.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述探讨了生命早期的 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 感染是否会导致儿童反复喘息或哮喘 (RW/A),重点关注因果关系、共同的遗传倾向和不同的临床轨迹。核心问题是在基于全国登记的 队列研究 中解决严重 RSV 感染(1 岁之前住院)和 RW/A(1 岁至 7 岁之间的药物报销)之间的关联。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述综合了芬兰一项全国性登记研究(1998-2014 年)的证据,该研究将登记数据与北欧遗传 队列研究 相结合。它包括一项针对六个北欧 队列研究(3,107 例病例,92,091 名对照)的 基因组 全关联研究 (GWAS) 和使用 155 种哮喘相关变异的两样本孟德尔随机化 (2SMR)。审查没有明确报告资格标准、检索日期或超出所描述的 队列研究 的数据库。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该综述得出的结论是,与没有 RSV 住院的 RW/A 相比,RSV 相关的 RW/A 表现出独特的临床特征,包括 1-2 岁时吸入药物使用量较高,但 5 岁后使用量较低,平均血液嗜酸性粒细胞较低(0.341 vs 0.398 x109/L;p=0.008)。兄弟姐妹对照分析显示 RSV 住院治疗与 RW/A 之间存在关联(OR 2.8;95% CI 2.4-3.2),尽管未受影响的兄弟姐妹的 RW/A 患病率 也升高。GWAS 在 APBB1IP 上发现了 RSV 关联(rs787036;β=0.209;p=8.80x10−8),并且 2SMR 没有发现证据表明哮喘遗传倾向影响 RSV 易感性。

analysis_en.scope_and_question: The review examines whether early-life respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection causes childhood recurrent wheeze or asthma (RW/A), focusing on causality, shared genetic liability, and distinct clinical trajectories. The central question addresses the association between severe RSV infection (hospitalisation before age 1 year) and RW/A (medication reimbursement between ages 1 and 7 years) in a nationwide registry-based cohort.
analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review synthesizes evidence from a nationwide registry-based study in Finland (1998–2014) combining registry data with Nordic genetic cohorts. It includes a genome-wide association study (GWAS) across six Nordic cohorts (3,107 cases, 92,091 controls) and two-sample Mendelian randomisation (2SMR) using 155 asthma-associated variants. The review does not explicitly report eligibility criteria, search dates, or databases beyond the described cohorts.
analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that RSV-associated RW/A exhibits distinct clinical features, including higher inhaled medication use at ages 1–2 years but lower use after age 5, and lower mean blood eosinophils (0.341 vs 0.398 x109/L; p=0.008) compared to RW/A without RSV hospitalisation. Sibling-controlled analyses show an association between RSV hospitalisation and RW/A (OR 2.8; 95% CI 2.4–3.2), though unaffected siblings also had elevated RW/A prevalence. GWAS identified an RSV association at APBB1IP (rs787036; β=0.209; p=8.80x10−8), and 2SMR found no evidence that asthma genetic liability influences RSV susceptibility.
analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights unresolved questions about the causal pathway between RSV and RW/A, as sibling analyses suggest potential unmeasured confounding despite familial controls. The distinct eosinophil trajectory in RSV-associated RW/A remains mechanistically unexplained, and the GWAS signal at APBB1IP requires further validation and functional studies to clarify its role in RSV susceptibility.
analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: The review prioritises long-term outcome monitoring in RSV prevention trials to assess whether reducing severe RSV infections mitigates RW/A risk. It also calls for mechanistic studies to elucidate the eosinophil trajectory differences and functional validation of the APBB1IP locus to determine its biological relevance to RSV susceptibility.

papers.title_zh: 婴儿 呼吸道合胞病毒 和儿童哮喘:一项基于全国登记、兄弟姐妹对照、基因组 范围的关联研究
papers.source_body_en: BackgroundEarly-life respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection is associated with childhood recurrent wheeze or asthma (RW/A), but causality and shared genetic liability remain unclear. MethodsWe combined Finnish nationwide registries and Nordic genetic cohorts. First, in 965 312 Finnish children born between 1998 and 2014, we defined severe RSV as RSV hospitalisation before age 1 year, and recurrent wheezing or asthma (RW/A) as inhaled medication reimbursement between ages 1 and 7 years, and compared medication and eosinophil trajectories by RSV history. Second, we assessed familial confounding in 527 776 full siblings and 15 667 RW/A- discordant pairs. Third, we performed a genome-wide association study (GWAS) of RSV susceptibility with meta-analysis across six Nordic cohorts (3 107 cases, 92 091 controls) and two-sample Mendelian randomisation (2SMR) using 155 asthma-associated variants. FindingsRSV-associated RW/A showed higher inhaled medication use at ages 1-2 years but lower use after age 5, and lower mean blood eosinophils (0{middle dot}341 vs 0{middle dot}398x10{square}/L; p=0{middle dot}008) than RW/A without RSV hospitalisation. In RW/A-discordant sibling pairs, RSV hospitalisation was associated with RW/A (OR 2{middle dot}8; 95% CI 2{middle dot}4-3{middle dot}2), while unaffected siblings also had elevated RW/A prevalence. GWAS identified an RSV association at APBB1IP (rs787036; {beta}=0{middle dot}209; p=8{middle dot}80x10-{square}). 2SMR provided no evidence that asthma genetic liability influenced RSV susceptibility. InterpretationThe RSV-asthma association is unlikely to be explained by shared genetic or environmental factors, and RSV-associated RW/A shows a distinct trajectory. These findings help prioritise long-term outcomes for RSV prevention trials and monitoring. FundingPaivikki and Sakari Sohlberg Foundation, Foundation for Pediatric Research, Sigrid Juselius Foundation, Orion Research Foundation, the Research Council of Norway.

papers.title: An evaluation of the anti-human respiratory syncytial virus activity of sophora alkaloids and the enhanced efficacy by liposomes via intratracheal administration
papers.abstract: Human respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major cause of severe lower respiratory tract infections and related deaths in infants, young children, and the elderly. The clinical management of RSV is challenging due to its high mutation rate and the limited efficacy and safety of existing antiviral drugs. Sophora alkaloids, natural compounds derived from Sophora flavescens, exhibit broad-spectrum antiviral and immunomodulatory activities. Mechanistically, RSV relies on ERK1/2 phosphorylation to facilitate viral replication and spread, while sophora alkaloids inhibit ERK1/2 phosphorylation via regulating MEK/ERK signaling pathway, thereby suppressing viral proliferation and the inflammatory response caused by RSV infection. In vivo studies demonstrated that sophora alkaloids significantly reduced the mortality of RSV-infected mice via intratracheal administration. To further enhance the pulmonary retention of drugs, liposomes were used to improve the therapeutic effects of sophora alkaloids. As the most effective sophora alkaloids against RSV infection, sophocarpine (SC) was encapsulated in liposomes to enhance its anti-RSV infection effect. In vivo studies demonstrate that SC-loaded liposomes outperformed the free SC in suppressing RSV replication and alleviating pulmonary inflammation in murine models of RSV infection. This study not only clarifies the mechanism by which sophora alkaloids counteract RSV-infection but also provides liposomal formulation of SC to improve the anti-RSV therapeutic effects.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Human respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) causes severe lower respiratory tract infections and deaths in infants, young children, and the elderly, while existing antiviral drugs have limited efficacy and safety. Sophora alkaloids, natural compounds with antiviral and immunomodulatory activities, may address this unmet need by targeting RSV replication and inflammation.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study evaluated the anti-RSV activity of sophora alkaloids and their liposomal formulations in murine models of RSV infection using intratracheal administration. Sophocarpine (SC), identified as the most effective alkaloid, was encapsulated in liposomes to enhance pulmonary retention and therapeutic effects.
analysis.methods: The study assessed RSV replication and pulmonary inflammation in mice treated with free SC or SC-loaded liposomes via intratracheal administration. Mechanistic investigations focused on the inhibition of ERK1/2 phosphorylation through regulation of the MEK/ERK signaling pathway to suppress viral proliferation and inflammatory responses.
analysis.main_results: In vivo studies showed that sophora alkaloids significantly reduced mortality in RSV-infected mice, and SC-loaded liposomes outperformed free SC in suppressing RSV replication and alleviating pulmonary inflammation in murine models.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study clarifies that sophora alkaloids counteract RSV infection by inhibiting ERK1/2 phosphorylation via the MEK/ERK pathway, and demonstrates that liposomal encapsulation of SC enhances its anti-RSV efficacy in vivo, representing a novel formulation strategy.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that liposomal formulations of sophora alkaloids, particularly SC, could improve therapeutic outcomes for RSV infection by enhancing pulmonary drug retention and antiviral activity, potentially addressing limitations of current treatments.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to murine models and does not report human clinical data, safety profiles, or comparative efficacy against standard-of-care antivirals, warranting cautious interpretation and further translational research.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the anti-human respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) activity of sophora alkaloids and evaluated the enhanced efficacy of sophocarpine (SC) when encapsulated in liposomes via intratracheal administration in murine models. RSV is a major cause of severe lower respiratory infections with limited treatment options, and sophora alkaloids were explored for their antiviral and immunomodulatory properties. Mechanistically, the alkaloids inhibit RSV replication by suppressing ERK1/2 phosphorylation through the MEK/ERK signaling pathway. In vivo, sophora alkaloids reduced mortality in RSV-infected mice, and SC-loaded liposomes outperformed free SC in reducing viral replication and pulmonary inflammation. The study highlights the potential of liposomal formulations to improve therapeutic outcomes for RSV infection, though findings are confined to animal models and lack human safety or efficacy data.

papers.title_zh: 槐生物碱的抗人呼吸道合胞病毒活性评价及脂质体气管内给药增强功效的评价
papers.source_body_en: Human respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major cause of severe lower respiratory tract infections and related deaths in infants, young children, and the elderly. The clinical management of RSV is challenging due to its high mutation rate and the limited efficacy and safety of existing antiviral drugs. Sophora alkaloids, natural compounds derived from Sophora flavescens, exhibit broad-spectrum antiviral and immunomodulatory activities. Mechanistically, RSV relies on ERK1/2 phosphorylation to facilitate viral replication and spread, while sophora alkaloids inhibit ERK1/2 phosphorylation via regulating MEK/ERK signaling pathway, thereby suppressing viral proliferation and the inflammatory response caused by RSV infection. In vivo studies demonstrated that sophora alkaloids significantly reduced the mortality of RSV-infected mice via intratracheal administration. To further enhance the pulmonary retention of drugs, liposomes were used to improve the therapeutic effects of sophora alkaloids. As the most effective sophora alkaloids against RSV infection, sophocarpine (SC) was encapsulated in liposomes to enhance its anti-RSV infection effect. In vivo studies demonstrate that SC-loaded liposomes outperformed the free SC in suppressing RSV replication and alleviating pulmonary inflammation in murine models of RSV infection. This study not only clarifies the mechanism by which sophora alkaloids counteract RSV-infection but also provides liposomal formulation of SC to improve the anti-RSV therapeutic effects.

papers.title: The Resurgence of Respiratory Viruses After COVID-19: Molecular Insights from Pediatric SARI in Kashmir.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Respiratory viruses are major contributors to severe acute respiratory infections (SARI) in children. Data on their molecular epidemiology in northern India remains limited, particularly in the post-COVID-19 period. This study aimed to determine the prevalence and distribution of respiratory viral pathogens among hospitalized pediatric SARI patients in Kashmir. METHODS: A prospective study was conducted from October 2023 to April 2025 at Sher-i-Kashmir Institute of Medical Sciences, Srinagar. Children aged ≤15 years meeting the World Health Organization SARI case definition were enrolled. Nasopharyngeal and/or oropharyngeal samples were collected and tested using real-time polymerase chain reaction assays for SARS-CoV-2, Influenza A and B, Respiratory Syncytial virus (RSV) A and B, Adenovirus, Human metapneumovirus, Rhinovirus, and Para-influenza viruses. RESULTS: A total of 326 pediatric SARI cases were included. At least one respiratory virus was detected in 200 patients (61.3%). RSV was the most frequently detected virus, with RSV-B identified in 111 cases (34.0%) and RSV-A in 26 cases (7.9%). Influenza viruses accounted for a smaller proportion, including influenza A(H1N1) in 12 cases (3.6%), influenza A(H3N2) in 6 cases (1.8%), and influenza B (Victoria lineage) in 21 cases (6.4%). Other viruses detected included Adenovirus, Para-influenza virus, Rhinovirus, and Human metapneumovirus. Most infections occurred during winter months and predominantly affected infants. CONCLUSION: Respiratory viruses account for a substantial proportion of pediatric SARI cases in Kashmir, with RSV emerging as the predominant pathogen in the post-pandemic period. Strengthening molecular surveillance may improve diagnostic stewardship and guide targeted prevention strategies.

papers.title_zh: COVID-19 后呼吸道病毒的死灰复燃:来自克什米尔儿科 SARI 的分子见解。
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Respiratory viruses are major contributors to severe acute respiratory infections (SARI) in children. Data on their molecular epidemiology in northern India remains limited, particularly in the post-COVID-19 period. This study aimed to determine the prevalence and distribution of respiratory viral pathogens among hospitalized pediatric SARI patients in Kashmir. METHODS: A prospective study was conducted from October 2023 to April 2025 at Sher-i-Kashmir Institute of Medical Sciences, Srinagar. Children aged ≤15 years meeting the World Health Organization SARI case definition were enrolled. Nasopharyngeal and/or oropharyngeal samples were collected and tested using real-time polymerase chain reaction assays for SARS-CoV-2, Influenza A and B, Respiratory Syncytial virus (RSV) A and B, Adenovirus, Human metapneumovirus, Rhinovirus, and Para-influenza viruses. RESULTS: A total of 326 pediatric SARI cases were included. At least one respiratory virus was detected in 200 patients (61.3%). RSV was the most frequently detected virus, with RSV-B identified in 111 cases (34.0%) and RSV-A in 26 cases (7.9%). Influenza viruses accounted for a smaller proportion, including influenza A(H1N1) in 12 cases (3.6%), influenza A(H3N2) in 6 cases (1.8%), and influenza B (Victoria lineage) in 21 cases (6.4%). Other viruses detected included Adenovirus, Para-influenza virus, Rhinovirus, and Human metapneumovirus. Most infections occurred during winter months and predominantly affected infants. CONCLUSION: Respiratory viruses account for a substantial proportion of pediatric SARI cases in Kashmir, with RSV emerging as the predominant pathogen in the post-pandemic period. Strengthening molecular surveillance may improve diagnostic stewardship and guide targeted prevention strategies.

papers.title: NonPharmaceutical Interventions and PostPandemic Resurgence: The Shifting Epidemiology of Influenza, Respiratory Syncytial Virus, and Adenovirus in Hangzhou, Zhejiang Province (2020-2024)
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Acute respiratory infections (ARIs) caused by influenza A/B (Flu A/Flu B), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and adenovirus (ADV) remain a major global health burden. The COVID-19 pandemic profoundly altered respiratory virus transmission through nonpharmaceutical interventions (NPIs). Methods Samples from patients with respiratory tract infections at Hangzhou Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine from January 2020 to October 2024 were collected. ADV, Flu A, Flu B, and RSV were detected to evaluate the impact of NPIs on viral epidemiology. Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS software and GraphPad Prism. Multivariable binary logistic regression models, adjusting for age group and sex, were constructed to evaluate the independent effect of NPI relaxation (strict NPI period 2020-2022 vs. post-relaxation period 2023-2024) on virus positivity. Stratified analyses by age group and demographic comparability assessments between periods were also performed. Results Overall virus positivity declined from 27.4% (2020) to 14.5% (2021) during strict NPIs, then rebounded to 35.1% in 2023 after relaxation. Flu A resurged atypically in summer 2022 and dominated the 2023 winter peak, while Flu B increased annually and peaked in 2024. ADV regained its prepandemic summer seasonality by 2024, whereas RSV showed limited seasonal variation. Higher ADV positivity was observed in males, and higher Flu B positivity in females. By 2024, influenza burden shifted toward adults and geriatric populations, while children under five remained most vulnerable to RSV and ADV. However, after adjusting for demographic shifts—including a significant increase in adult patients (18-60 years: 22.1% to 40.0%) and altered sex ratios between periods (both P 0.05). Stratified analyses further revealed that the magnitude of period-related risk reduction increased with age for all pathogens. Conclusion This study demonstrates that the postpandemic resurgence of respiratory viruses in Hangzhou, Zhejiang Province, was not a monolithic recrudescence following NPIs relaxation, but a multifaceted shifting epidemiology driven by three convergent forces: expanded school-based and community screening that broadened the tested denominator, demographic case-mix shifts toward higher-risk adult populations, and pathogen-specific alterations in seasonal and age-specific transmission patterns. The consistently lower adjusted odds of positivity during the post-relaxation period indicate that crude resurgence signals must be interpreted through the lens of surveillance structure.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed why nonpharmaceutical interventions (NPIs) during the COVID-19 pandemic altered the epidemiology of influenza A/B, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and adenovirus (ADV), and how their relaxation reshaped postpandemic transmission patterns in Hangzhou, Zhejiang Province.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This was a retrospective observational study analyzing respiratory virus detections in patients with respiratory tract infections at Hangzhou Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine from January 2020 to October 2024, comparing periods of strict NPIs (2020–2022) with post-relaxation (2023–2024).
analysis.methods: Multivariable binary logistic regression models adjusted for age group and sex were used to evaluate the independent effect of NPI relaxation on virus positivity, with stratified analyses by age group and demographic comparability assessments between periods.
analysis.main_results: Overall virus positivity declined from 27.4% in 2020 to 14.5% in 2021 during strict NPIs, then rebounded to 35.1% in 2023 after relaxation. Flu A resurged atypically in summer 2022 and dominated the 2023 winter peak, while Flu B increased annually and peaked in 2024. ADV regained prepandemic summer seasonality by 2024, whereas RSV showed limited seasonal variation.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the postpandemic resurgence as a multifaceted shift driven by expanded screening, demographic shifts toward higher-risk adult populations, and pathogen-specific changes in seasonality and age-specific transmission, rather than a uniform recrudescence following NPI relaxation.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings caution that crude resurgence signals must be interpreted with surveillance structure adjustments, highlighting the need for age-stratified and pathogen-specific surveillance to inform targeted prevention and control strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s single-center design, reliance on hospital-based samples, and lack of randomization limit causal inference and generalizability, warranting cautious interpretation of the adjusted odds ratios and demographic shifts.

analysis.summary_en: This study examined how nonpharmaceutical interventions (NPIs) during the COVID-19 pandemic altered the epidemiology of influenza A/B, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and adenovirus (ADV) in Hangzhou, Zhejiang Province, and how their relaxation reshaped postpandemic transmission from 2020 to 2024. Using multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age and sex, the authors analyzed respiratory virus detections in hospital patients and found that overall virus positivity declined during strict NPIs (27.4% in 2020 to 14.5% in 2021) but rebounded to 35.1% in 2023 after relaxation. Pathogen-specific patterns emerged: Flu A resurged atypically in summer 2022 and dominated the 2023 winter peak, Flu B increased annually peaking in 2024, ADV regained prepandemic summer seasonality by 2024, and RSV showed limited seasonal variation. The authors attribute the resurgence to expanded screening, demographic shifts toward higher-risk adults, and pathogen-specific transmission changes rather than a uniform recrudescence. They emphasize that surveillance systems must account for these factors to avoid misinterpreting crude resurgence signals. However, the single-center design and reliance on hospital-based samples limit generalizability and causal inference.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究探讨了为什么 COVID-19 大流行期间的非药物干预 (NPI) 改变了 A/B 型流感、呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 和腺病毒 (ADV) 的 流行病学,以及它们的放松如何重塑了浙江省杭州市大流行后的 传播 模式。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这是一项回顾性观察性研究,分析了杭州市中医院 2020 年 1 月至 2024 年 10 月期间呼吸道感染患者的呼吸道病毒检测情况,并将严格 NPI 期间(2020-2022 年)与放松后(2023-2024 年)进行比较。
elements_zh.methods: 使用针对年龄组和性别进行调整的多变量二元逻辑回归模型来评估 NPI 放宽对病毒阳性率的独立影响,并按年龄组进行分层分析,并进行各时期之间的人口统计学可比性评估。
elements_zh.main_results: 在严格的 NPI 期间,总体病毒阳性率从 2020 年的 27.4% 下降至 2021 年的 14.5%,然后在放松后于 2023 年反弹至 35.1%。A 型流感在 2022 年夏季非典型地卷土重来,并主导了 2023 年冬季高峰,而 B 型流感则逐年增加,并于 2024 年达到高峰。ADV 到 2024 年恢复了大流行前的夏季季节性,而 RSV 则表现出有限的季节性变化。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将大流行后的复苏解释为由扩大筛查、人口结构向高风险成年人群的转变以及季节性和特定年龄 传播 的病原体特异性变化驱动的多方面转变,而不是 NPI 放松后的统一复发。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果警告说,粗略的复苏信号必须通过 监测 结构调整来解释,强调需要按年龄分层和病原体特异性 监测 来为有针对性的预防和控制策略提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的单中心设计、对医院样本的依赖以及缺乏随机性限制了因果推断和普遍性,需要对调整后的比值比和人口变化进行谨慎解释。

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要背景 由甲型/乙型流感(Flu A/Flu B)、呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 和腺病毒 (ADV) 引起的急性呼吸道感染 (ARIs) 仍然是全球主要的健康负担。COVID-19 大流行通过非药物干预措施 (NPI) 深刻改变了呼吸道病毒 传播。方法收集2020年1月至2024年10月杭州市中医院收治的呼吸道感染患者标本。检测 ADV、Flu A、Flu B 和 RSV,以评估 NPI 对病毒 流行病学 的影响。使用SPSS软件和GraphPad Prism进行统计分析。构建了调整年龄组和性别的多变量二元逻辑回归模型,以评估 NPI 放宽(2020-2022 年严格 NPI 期与 2023-2024 年放宽后期)对病毒阳性的独立影响。还进行了按年龄组的分层分析和不同时期之间的人口可比性评估。结果 在严格的 NPI 期间,总体病毒阳性率从 27.4%(2020 年)下降至 14.5%(2021 年),然后在放松后于 2023 年反弹至 35.1%。A 型流感在 2022 年夏季非典型地卷土重来,并主导了 2023 年冬季高峰,而 B 型流感则逐年增加,并于 2024 年达到高峰。ADV 到 2024 年恢复了大流行前的夏季季节性,而 RSV 则表现出有限的季节性变化。男性中 ADV 阳性率较高,女性中 B 型流感阳性率较高。到 2024 年,流感负担转向成人和老年人群,而五岁以下儿童仍然最容易感染 RSV 和 ADV。然而,在对人口统计变化进行调整后,包括成年患者的显着增加(18-60 岁:22.1% 至 40.0%)以及不同时期之间性别比例的变化(均 P < 0.05)。分层分析进一步显示,对于所有病原体来说,与经期相关的风险降低幅度随着年龄的增长而增加。结论 本研究表明,浙江省杭州市大流行后呼吸道病毒的死灰复燃并不是 NPI 放松后的整体复发,而是由三种汇聚力量驱动的 流行病学 的多方面转变:扩大学校和社区筛查,扩大了测试分母,人口统计病例组合向高风险成年人群转变,以及季节性和特定年龄 传播 模式的病原体特异性改变。松弛后期间调整后的阳性几率持续较低,表明必须通过 监测 结构的透镜来解释粗略的复苏信号。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究探讨了为什么 COVID-19 大流行期间的非药物干预 (NPI) 改变了 A/B 型流感、呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 和腺病毒 (ADV) 的 流行病学,以及它们的放松如何重塑了浙江省杭州市大流行后的 传播 模式。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 这是一项回顾性观察性研究,分析了杭州市中医院 2020 年 1 月至 2024 年 10 月期间呼吸道感染患者的呼吸道病毒检测情况,并将严格 NPI 期间(2020-2022 年)与放松后(2023-2024 年)进行比较。
analysis_zh.methods: 使用针对年龄组和性别进行调整的多变量二元逻辑回归模型来评估 NPI 放宽对病毒阳性率的独立影响,并按年龄组进行分层分析,并进行各时期之间的人口统计学可比性评估。
analysis_zh.main_results: 在严格的 NPI 期间,总体病毒阳性率从 2020 年的 27.4% 下降至 2021 年的 14.5%,然后在放松后于 2023 年反弹至 35.1%。A 型流感在 2022 年夏季非典型地卷土重来,并主导了 2023 年冬季高峰,而 B 型流感则逐年增加,并于 2024 年达到高峰。ADV 到 2024 年恢复了大流行前的夏季季节性,而 RSV 则表现出有限的季节性变化。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将大流行后的复苏解释为由扩大筛查、人口结构向高风险成年人群的转变以及季节性和特定年龄 传播 的病原体特异性变化驱动的多方面转变,而不是 NPI 放松后的统一复发。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果警告说,粗略的复苏信号必须通过 监测 结构调整来解释,强调需要按年龄分层和病原体特异性 监测 来为有针对性的预防和控制策略提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的单中心设计、对医院样本的依赖以及缺乏随机性限制了因果推断和普遍性,需要对调整后的比值比和人口变化进行谨慎解释。

papers.title: Comparison of the protective effect of human respiratory syncytial virus Pre-F protein combined with different adjuvants in BALB/c mice
papers.abstract: Introduction Human respiratory syncytial virus (HRSV) has a high disease burden in infants and elderly individuals. In this study, the adjuvants AlOH, AlOH+CpG and BFA03 were used to compare the protective effect of HRSV prefusion protein (Pre-F) in BALB/c mice. Methods We divided BALB/c mice into three experimental groups (Pre-F+AlOH+CpG, Pre-F+AlOH, and Pre-F+BFA03) and three adjuvant control groups (AlOH+CpG, AlOH, and BFA03). After two intramuscular immunizations, we measured serum neutralizing antibody titers and quantified the numbers of IFN-γ- and IL-4-secreting lymphocytes. After viral challenge, we monitored body weight changes, determined lung viral loads (Ct values), and scored lung pathological damage. Results The mice in the experimental groups exhibited high titres of neutralizing antibodies and increased numbers of IFN-γ- and IL-4-secreting lymphocytes. The mice began to regain weight on the third day after challenge, but the mice in the adjuvant groups continued to lose weight. The mice immunized with Pre-F+BFA03 elicited the highest neutralizing antibody titre (1716), the lowest viral load in the lung, and milder pathological damage. The mice immunized with Pre-F+AlOH had the most severe lung pathological injury (score: 2.83) and the highest viral load in the lung (Ct value: 32.2). Compared with the BFA03 adjuvant, the AlOH adjuvant induced a Th2-biased humoral immune response in mice. The Pre-F+AlOH+CpG group had the least pathological damage in the lung (score 2.16), and the ability to induce neutralizing antibodies and cellular immune responses was comparable with that of the BFA03 adjuvant. Discussion These findings indicate that Pre-F protein combined with AlOH+CpG or BFA03 adjuvant provided similar protection in mice and both were superior to the AlOH adjuvant, providing a reference for adjuvant selection and formulation strategies in HRSV Pre-F protein vaccine development.

papers.source_body_en: Introduction Human respiratory syncytial virus (HRSV) has a high disease burden in infants and elderly individuals. In this study, the adjuvants AlOH, AlOH+CpG and BFA03 were used to compare the protective effect of HRSV prefusion protein (Pre-F) in BALB/c mice. Methods We divided BALB/c mice into three experimental groups (Pre-F+AlOH+CpG, Pre-F+AlOH, and Pre-F+BFA03) and three adjuvant control groups (AlOH+CpG, AlOH, and BFA03). After two intramuscular immunizations, we measured serum neutralizing antibody titers and quantified the numbers of IFN-γ- and IL-4-secreting lymphocytes. After viral challenge, we monitored body weight changes, determined lung viral loads (Ct values), and scored lung pathological damage. Results The mice in the experimental groups exhibited high titres of neutralizing antibodies and increased numbers of IFN-γ- and IL-4-secreting lymphocytes. The mice began to regain weight on the third day after challenge, but the mice in the adjuvant groups continued to lose weight. The mice immunized with Pre-F+BFA03 elicited the highest neutralizing antibody titre (1716), the lowest viral load in the lung, and milder pathological damage. The mice immunized with Pre-F+AlOH had the most severe lung pathological injury (score: 2.83) and the highest viral load in the lung (Ct value: 32.2). Compared with the BFA03 adjuvant, the AlOH adjuvant induced a Th2-biased humoral immune response in mice. The Pre-F+AlOH+CpG group had the least pathological damage in the lung (score 2.16), and the ability to induce neutralizing antibodies and cellular immune responses was comparable with that of the BFA03 adjuvant. Discussion These findings indicate that Pre-F protein combined with AlOH+CpG or BFA03 adjuvant provided similar protection in mice and both were superior to the AlOH adjuvant, providing a reference for adjuvant selection and formulation strategies in HRSV Pre-F protein vaccine development.

papers.title: Highly pathogenic porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus nonstructural protein 1 interacts with TRAF6 to activate the TAK1/p38/JNK/AP-1 signaling and induce IL-1β
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome (PRRS) caused by PRRS virus (PRRSV) is a highly contagious disease that severely threatens the global pig industry. A significant symptom of PRRS is severe pneumonia. At present, studies have shown that IL-1β is upregulated by PRRSV infection in vivo and in vitro , while the underlying mechanism remains unknown. Here, we explored how PRRSV regulated IL-1β production. We found that HP-PRRSV nsp1 upregulated the expression of IL-1β. Overexpression of nsp1 induced IL-1β production in a dose-dependent manner. Subsequently, we demonstrated that nsp1 enhanced IL-1β expression by activating JNK/p38 signaling pathways, as the addition of p38 and JNK inhibitors reduced IL-1β production induced by nsp1. Moreover, deleting the AP-1 binding motif in porcine IL-1β promoter impaired IL-1β expression induced by nsp1, suggesting that AP-1 is essential for IL-1β production. In addition, we showed that TRAF6 was required for nsp1 to activate the TAK1/JNK/p38/AP-1 signaling pathway by interacting with each other. Truncation and deletion mutation analysis indicated that R308 and R375 amino acids were important for nsp1 to interact with TRAF6 and induce IL-1β production. Finally, we constructed the recombinant viruses mutated at R308 and R375 and found that the mutated virus PRRSV-R308/375A exhibited a significantly reduced replication rate and impaired the ability to induce IL-1β compared to the wild-type strain. These findings provide new insights into the molecular mechanisms of IL-1β production induced by PRRSV and help us further understand the pathogenesis of PRRSV infection. IMPORTANCE Highly pathogenic porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus (HP-PRRSV) has been prevalent in China since 2006, causing severe pneumonia in pigs. IL-1β is a proinflammatory cytokine secreted by various cells. In this study, we demonstrated that PRRSV protein nsp1 interacted with TRAF6 to activate the TAK1/JNK/p38/AP-1 signaling pathway, consequently inducing the expression of IL-1β. Additionally, our findings revealed that R308 and R375 in nsp1 were critical amino acid residues for nsp1 to interact with TRAF6 and induce IL-1β production. Notably, the recombinant virus PRRSV-R308/375A exhibited a significantly reduced replication rate and impaired ability to induce proinflammatory cytokines in vitro compared to the wild-type strain HP-PRRSV. This study helps us further understand HP-PRRSV pathogenesis and provides a new idea for the development of PRRSV vaccines.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates how highly pathogenic porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus (HP-PRRSV) induces IL-1β production, a proinflammatory cytokine upregulated during infection. The research demonstrates that the viral nonstructural protein 1 (nsp1) interacts with TRAF6 to activate the TAK1/p38/JNK/AP-1 signaling pathway, driving IL-1β expression. Key findings include the dose-dependent induction of IL-1β by nsp1, the necessity of p38 and JNK pathways, and the critical role of AP-1 in promoter activation. papers.title_zh: 高致病性猪繁殖与呼吸综合征病毒非结构蛋白1与TRAF6相互作用激活TAK1/p38/JNK/AP-1信号并诱导IL-1β
papers.source_body_en: ABSTRACT Porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome (PRRS) caused by PRRS virus (PRRSV) is a highly contagious disease that severely threatens the global pig industry. A significant symptom of PRRS is severe pneumonia. At present, studies have shown that IL-1β is upregulated by PRRSV infection in vivo and in vitro , while the underlying mechanism remains unknown. Here, we explored how PRRSV regulated IL-1β production. We found that HP-PRRSV nsp1 upregulated the expression of IL-1β. Overexpression of nsp1 induced IL-1β production in a dose-dependent manner. Subsequently, we demonstrated that nsp1 enhanced IL-1β expression by activating JNK/p38 signaling pathways, as the addition of p38 and JNK inhibitors reduced IL-1β production induced by nsp1. Moreover, deleting the AP-1 binding motif in porcine IL-1β promoter impaired IL-1β expression induced by nsp1, suggesting that AP-1 is essential for IL-1β production. In addition, we showed that TRAF6 was required for nsp1 to activate the TAK1/JNK/p38/AP-1 signaling pathway by interacting with each other. Truncation and deletion mutation analysis indicated that R308 and R375 amino acids were important for nsp1 to interact with TRAF6 and induce IL-1β production. Finally, we constructed the recombinant viruses mutated at R308 and R375 and found that the mutated virus PRRSV-R308/375A exhibited a significantly reduced replication rate and impaired the ability to induce IL-1β compared to the wild-type strain. These findings provide new insights into the molecular mechanisms of IL-1β production induced by PRRSV and help us further understand the pathogenesis of PRRSV infection. IMPORTANCE Highly pathogenic porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus (HP-PRRSV) has been prevalent in China since 2006, causing severe pneumonia in pigs. IL-1β is a proinflammatory cytokine secreted by various cells. In this study, we demonstrated that PRRSV protein nsp1 interacted with TRAF6 to activate the TAK1/JNK/p38/AP-1 signaling pathway, consequently inducing the expression of IL-1β. Additionally, our findings revealed that R308 and R375 in nsp1 were critical amino acid residues for nsp1 to interact with TRAF6 and induce IL-1β production. Notably, the recombinant virus PRRSV-R308/375A exhibited a significantly reduced replication rate and impaired ability to induce proinflammatory cytokines in vitro compared to the wild-type strain HP-PRRSV. This study helps us further understand HP-PRRSV pathogenesis and provides a new idea for the development of PRRSV vaccines.

papers.title: Global Research Trends in Respiratory Syncytial Virus Vaccine Research: A Bibliometric Analysis
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major cause of acute respiratory infections and has long posed challenges to vaccine development because of historical safety concerns and the complexity of protective immunity. Recent advances in structural biology, maternal immunization, vaccines for older adults, and monoclonal antibodies have reshaped this field. This study aimed to analyze global research trends in RSV vaccine research using a bibliometric approach. Methods: A bibliometric study was conducted using records retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection on April 1, 2026. Original articles and reviews published between 1968 and 2026 were selected through a title-based search strategy related to RSV and vaccination. Bibliometric indicators, citation patterns, collaboration networks, source distribution, and thematic structures were analyzed using Bibliometrix and Biblioshiny in R. Results: The final sample included 1,455 documents from 394 sources, with an annual growth rate of 8.7%. Scientific production increased markedly after 2010, with stronger acceleration after 2020. The United States led global output, followed by China, the United Kingdom, Canada, and the Netherlands. Vaccine was the most productive and locally influential source. Citation analysis identified the formalin-inactivated RSV vaccine studies from 1969 and the prefusion F protein study from 2013 as major intellectual milestones. Keyword analysis showed a shift from disease burden, epidemiology, and pathogenesis toward immunization, immunogenicity, maternal vaccination, older adults, and monoclonal antibodies. Conclusions: RSV vaccine research has evolved from a historically safety-constrained field to a mature translational area focused on prevention, implementation, real-world effectiveness, and equitable access.
authors: Andréia Rodrigues Moura da Costa Valle

papers.abstract_zh: 背景/目标:呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 是急性呼吸道感染的主要原因,并且由于历史安全问题和保护性免疫的复杂性,长期以来对 疫苗 的开发构成挑战。结构生物学、母体免疫、老年人 疫苗 和单克隆抗体的最新进展重塑了这一领域。本研究旨在使用文献计量方法分析 RSV 疫苗 研究的全球研究趋势。方法:使用 2026 年 4 月 1 日从 Web of Science 核心合集中检索的记录进行文献计量研究。通过与 RSV 和 疫苗接种 相关的基于标题的搜索策略选择 1968 年至 2026 年间发表的原创文章和评论。使用 R 中的 Bibliometrix 和 Biblioshiny 分析文献计量指标、引用模式、协作网络、来源分布和主题结构。结果:最终样本包括来自 394 个来源的 1,455 篇文献,年增长率为 8.7%。科学产出在 2010 年之后显着增长,2020 年之后加速加速。美国引领全球产出,其次是中国、英国、加拿大和荷兰。疫苗 是最具生产力和当地影响力的来源。引文分析将 1969 年的福尔马林灭活 RSV 疫苗 研究和 2013 年的预融合 F 蛋白研究确定为主要的智力里程碑。关键词分析显示,从疾病负担、流行病学 和 发病机制 转向免疫、免疫原性、母体 疫苗接种、老年人和单克隆抗体。结论:RSV 疫苗 研究已从历史上安全受限的领域发展成为专注于预防、实施、现实世界有效性和公平获取的成熟转化领域。

papers.full_text: Abstract Introduction: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs) in infants and young children. This study evaluated clinical and laboratory factors associated with prolonged hospitalization in pediatric RSV infection. Methods: This retrospective study included children under 18 years of age hospitalized with LRTI and confirmed RSV infection at our center between 2023 and 2025. Demographic, clinical, and laboratory data were collected from hospital records. Patients were divided into two groups according to length of stay (LOS): ≤2 days and >2 days. Multivariate logistic regression analysis was performed using the backward stepwise method. Results: A total of 185 RSV-infected children were analyzed. The median age was 2 months, and 51.9% were male. Patients with LOS >2 days had significantly higher rates of PICU admission, non-invasive ventilation, mechanical ventilation, and secondary bacterial infections. Laboratory findings showed higher lymphocyte counts and BUN levels in the prolonged-stay group, whereas MPV levels were lower. No mortality was observed. In the multivariate logistic regression analysis, PICU stay was associated with approximately 12-fold increased risk of hospitalization longer than 2 days. Conclusion: Hospitalization longer than 2 days was associated with a more severe clinical course. In the multivariate logistic regression analysis, PICU stay was the main factor associated with hospitalization longer than 2 days. Lymphocyte count, MPV, and BUN may provide supportive clinical information; however, their independent prognostic value remains uncertain.

analysis.research_question_and_background: RSV is a leading cause of lower respiratory tract infections in infants and young children, yet predictors of prolonged hospitalization remain insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to identify clinical and laboratory factors associated with hospitalization exceeding 2 days in pediatric RSV infections.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective study enrolled children under 18 years hospitalized with laboratory-confirmed RSV lower respiratory tract infection at a single center between 2023 and 2025. Patients were stratified by length of stay (≤2 days vs >2 days) for comparative analysis.
analysis.methods: Demographic, clinical, and laboratory data were abstracted from hospital records. Multivariate logistic regression with backward stepwise selection was used to identify predictors of prolonged hospitalization (>2 days).
analysis.main_results: Among 185 RSV-infected children, the median age was 2 months and 51.9% were male. Patients with prolonged hospitalization (>2 days) had higher rates of PICU admission, non-invasive ventilation, mechanical ventilation, and secondary bacterial infections. Laboratory findings showed higher lymphocyte counts and BUN levels, while MPV levels were lower in the prolonged-stay group. No mortality occurred.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret prolonged hospitalization as reflecting a more severe clinical course in pediatric RSV infection. They highlight PICU stay as the dominant predictor of extended hospitalization and suggest that lymphocyte count, MPV, and BUN may offer supportive prognostic information, though their independent value remains uncertain.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings may inform risk stratification and resource allocation for pediatric RSV hospitalizations by identifying patients at risk of prolonged stays. The identified associations could guide clinical monitoring and early intervention strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The single-center retrospective design and absence of external validation limit generalizability and causal inference. The evidence is assessed as moderate due to potential unmeasured confounding and the uncertain independent prognostic value of laboratory markers.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective study of 185 children hospitalized with RSV lower respiratory tract infection between 2023 and 2025 identified factors associated with prolonged hospitalization (>2 days). Patients with extended stays had higher rates of intensive care, ventilatory support, and secondary bacterial infections, alongside elevated lymphocyte counts and BUN, and lower MPV. Multivariate analysis indicated that PICU stay was associated with a 12-fold increased risk of prolonged hospitalization, while lymphocyte count, MPV, and BUN showed supportive but uncertain prognostic value. The study suggests that clinical severity markers may aid risk stratification, though single-center design and retrospective data limit generalizability and causal conclusions.

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: RSV is a leading cause of lower respiratory tract infections in infants and young children, yet predictors of prolonged hospitalization remain insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to identify clinical and laboratory factors associated with hospitalization exceeding 2 days in pediatric RSV infections.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: A retrospective study enrolled children under 18 years hospitalized with laboratory-confirmed RSV lower respiratory tract infection at a single center between 2023 and 2025. Patients were stratified by length of stay (≤2 days vs >2 days) for comparative analysis.
analysis_en.methods: Demographic, clinical, and laboratory data were abstracted from hospital records. Multivariate logistic regression with backward stepwise selection was used to identify predictors of prolonged hospitalization (>2 days).
analysis_en.main_results: Among 185 RSV-infected children, the median age was 2 months and 51.9% were male. Patients with prolonged hospitalization (>2 days) had higher rates of PICU admission, non-invasive ventilation, mechanical ventilation, and secondary bacterial infections. Laboratory findings showed higher lymphocyte counts and BUN levels, while MPV levels were lower in the prolonged-stay group. No mortality occurred.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret prolonged hospitalization as reflecting a more severe clinical course in pediatric RSV infection. They highlight PICU stay as the dominant predictor of extended hospitalization and suggest that lymphocyte count, MPV, and BUN may offer supportive prognostic information, though their independent value remains uncertain.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings may inform risk stratification and resource allocation for pediatric RSV hospitalizations by identifying patients at risk of prolonged stays. The identified associations could guide clinical monitoring and early intervention strategies.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The single-center retrospective design and absence of external validation limit generalizability and causal inference. The evidence is assessed as moderate due to potential unmeasured confounding and the uncertain independent prognostic value of laboratory markers.

papers.title: RSV can infect the human nasal epithelium via the basolateral route and shows distinct subgroup infectivity and basal cell tropism
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) causes millions of lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs) in young children, older adults, and immunocompromised populations every year. RSV infection initiates in the upper respiratory tract and can progress to the lower airways, resulting in bronchiolitis, pneumonia, and even death. RSV primarily infects epithelial cells apically, but we hypothesized that basolateral exposure of the respiratory epithelium could provide an alternative mechanism of infection that contributes to LRTI development. Using a human nose organoid-air-liquid interface (HNO-ALI) model, we performed apical and basolateral inoculations with contemporaneous RSV strains (RSV/A/Ontario [RSV/A/ON] and RSV/B/Buenos Aires [RSV/B/BA]) representing the two RSV subgroups (A and B) in both adult- and infant-derived HNO-ALIs. Basolateral RSV exposure resulted in delayed viral replication and apical release compared to apical infection. A statistically significant difference in basolateral infection frequency was observed between RSV/B/BA and RSV/A/ON (81.3% versus 25%). Basolateral infection selectively targeted a rare basal cell population, while preserving epithelial integrity. Using undifferentiated HNO-ALIs, we determined for the first time that Krt23+ activated basal cells are uniquely susceptible to RSV infection, a finding we confirmed in fully differentiated HNO-ALIs. Together, our findings show that RSV can infect the respiratory epithelium from the basolateral side by initially targeting a rare subset of basal cells before spreading apically to ciliated cells. Moreover, RSV/B/BA may have an advantage over RSV/A/ON in utilizing the basolateral infection route. These findings highlight an alternative RSV infection pathway and could be a potential mechanism for RSV spread to the lower airways. IMPORTANCE Understanding the pathogenesis of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is essential to understanding and preventing acute and long-term sequelae from infection. The canonical understanding of RSV infection is that the virus infects and is restricted to the apical ciliated cells upon inhalation or fomite exposure. We demonstrate that an alternative route of infection—the basolateral route—can be utilized by RSV to infect the apical ciliated cells of the respiratory epithelium. We also show for the first time a novel difference in infectivity between the two contemporaneous RSV strains (RSV/A/Ontario and RSV/B/Buenos Aires). In addition, we describe a rare basal subset—the Krt23+ activated basal cells—that are uniquely susceptible to RSV, expanding the known cellular tropism of RSV. Infection of basal cells can impact airway differentiation, homeostasis, and remodeling. Overall, our findings expand on RSV pathogenesis and indicate there are alternative mechanisms of infection and cell populations that are susceptible to RSV.
