analysis.research_question_and_background: RSV causes substantial morbidity in young children, older adults, and immunocompromised populations, yet the canonical apical infection route does not fully explain progression to severe lower respiratory tract disease. The study addressed a knowledge gap by asking whether basolateral exposure of the respiratory epithelium provides an alternative mechanism of RSV infection that could contribute to lower airway involvement.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used human nose organoid-air-liquid interface (HNO-ALI) models derived from both adult and infant tissues to test RSV infection via apical and basolateral routes. Contemporaneous RSV strains from subgroups A (RSV/A/Ontario) and B (RSV/B/Buenos Aires) were inoculated in parallel.
analysis.methods: Apical and basolateral inoculations were performed using RSV/A/ON and RSV/B/BA in adult- and infant-derived HNO-ALIs. Infection dynamics were compared between routes and subgroups, and Krt23+ activated basal cell susceptibility was assessed in undifferentiated and fully differentiated HNO-ALIs.
analysis.main_results: Basolateral RSV exposure led to delayed viral replication and apical release compared to apical infection. RSV/B/BA showed a significantly higher basolateral infection frequency than RSV/A/ON (81.3% versus 25%). Basolateral infection selectively targeted a rare basal cell population (Krt23+ activated basal cells) while preserving epithelial integrity.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret these findings as evidence that RSV can infect the respiratory epithelium via the basolateral route by initially targeting Krt23+ activated basal cells before spreading apically to ciliated cells. They report a novel difference in basolateral infectivity between RSV subgroups A and B and identify a previously unrecognized basal cell tropism.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest an alternative RSV infection pathway that may facilitate spread to the lower airways, potentially informing surveillance strategies and the development of interventions targeting basal cell infection or basolateral entry.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro HNO-ALI models and does not assess in vivo relevance or clinical outcomes, which constrains the generalisability of the findings. The evidence is moderate due to the absence of animal or human challenge data and reliance on a single experimental system.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated whether respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) can infect human nasal epithelium via the basolateral route, addressing a gap in understanding RSV pathogenesis beyond the canonical apical infection pathway. Using human nose organoid-air-liquid interface models derived from adult and infant tissues, the authors compared apical and basolateral inoculations with contemporaneous RSV strains from subgroups A (RSV/A/Ontario) and B (RSV/B/Buenos Aires). Basolateral exposure resulted in delayed viral replication and apical release, with RSV/B/BA showing a significantly higher basolateral infection frequency (81.3%) than RSV/A/ON (25%). Infection selectively targeted Krt23+ activated basal cells while preserving epithelial integrity, indicating a previously unrecognized basal cell tropism. The authors propose that basolateral infection may represent an alternative route enabling RSV spread to the lower airways. While the findings expand understanding of RSV cellular tropism and subgroup-specific infectivity, the in vitro nature of the study and lack of in vivo validation limit direct clinical or public health implications.

elements_en.research_question_and_background: RSV causes substantial morbidity in young children, older adults, and immunocompromised populations, yet the canonical apical infection route does not fully explain progression to severe lower respiratory tract disease. The study addressed a knowledge gap by asking whether basolateral exposure of the respiratory epithelium provides an alternative mechanism of RSV infection that could contribute to lower airway involvement.
elements_en.study_design_and_population: The study used human nose organoid-air-liquid interface (HNO-ALI) models derived from both adult and infant tissues to test RSV infection via apical and basolateral routes. Contemporaneous RSV strains from subgroups A (RSV/A/Ontario) and B (RSV/B/Buenos Aires) were inoculated in parallel.
elements_en.methods: Apical and basolateral inoculations were performed using RSV/A/ON and RSV/B/BA in adult- and infant-derived HNO-ALIs. Infection dynamics were compared between routes and subgroups, and Krt23+ activated basal cell susceptibility was assessed in undifferentiated and fully differentiated HNO-ALIs.
elements_en.main_results: Basolateral RSV exposure led to delayed viral replication and apical release compared to apical infection. RSV/B/BA showed a significantly higher basolateral infection frequency than RSV/A/ON (81.3% versus 25%). Basolateral infection selectively targeted a rare basal cell population (Krt23+ activated basal cells) while preserving epithelial integrity.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret these findings as evidence that RSV can infect the respiratory epithelium via the basolateral route by initially targeting Krt23+ activated basal cells before spreading apically to ciliated cells. They report a novel difference in basolateral infectivity between RSV subgroups A and B and identify a previously unrecognized basal cell tropism.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest an alternative RSV infection pathway that may facilitate spread to the lower airways, potentially informing surveillance strategies and the development of interventions targeting basal cell infection or basolateral entry.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro HNO-ALI models and does not assess in vivo relevance or clinical outcomes, which constrains the generalisability of the findings. The evidence is moderate due to the absence of animal or human challenge data and reliance on a single experimental system.

papers.title_zh: RSV可通过基底外侧途径感染人鼻上皮,并表现出独特的亚群感染性和基底细胞向性
papers.source_body_en: ABSTRACT Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) causes millions of lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs) in young children, older adults, and immunocompromised populations every year. RSV infection initiates in the upper respiratory tract and can progress to the lower airways, resulting in bronchiolitis, pneumonia, and even death. RSV primarily infects epithelial cells apically, but we hypothesized that basolateral exposure of the respiratory epithelium could provide an alternative mechanism of infection that contributes to LRTI development. Using a human nose organoid-air-liquid interface (HNO-ALI) model, we performed apical and basolateral inoculations with contemporaneous RSV strains (RSV/A/Ontario [RSV/A/ON] and RSV/B/Buenos Aires [RSV/B/BA]) representing the two RSV subgroups (A and B) in both adult- and infant-derived HNO-ALIs. Basolateral RSV exposure resulted in delayed viral replication and apical release compared to apical infection. A statistically significant difference in basolateral infection frequency was observed between RSV/B/BA and RSV/A/ON (81.3% versus 25%). Basolateral infection selectively targeted a rare basal cell population, while preserving epithelial integrity. Using undifferentiated HNO-ALIs, we determined for the first time that Krt23+ activated basal cells are uniquely susceptible to RSV infection, a finding we confirmed in fully differentiated HNO-ALIs. Together, our findings show that RSV can infect the respiratory epithelium from the basolateral side by initially targeting a rare subset of basal cells before spreading apically to ciliated cells. Moreover, RSV/B/BA may have an advantage over RSV/A/ON in utilizing the basolateral infection route. These findings highlight an alternative RSV infection pathway and could be a potential mechanism for RSV spread to the lower airways. IMPORTANCE Understanding the pathogenesis of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is essential to understanding and preventing acute and long-term sequelae from infection. The canonical understanding of RSV infection is that the virus infects and is restricted to the apical ciliated cells upon inhalation or fomite exposure. We demonstrate that an alternative route of infection—the basolateral route—can be utilized by RSV to infect the apical ciliated cells of the respiratory epithelium. We also show for the first time a novel difference in infectivity between the two contemporaneous RSV strains (RSV/A/Ontario and RSV/B/Buenos Aires). In addition, we describe a rare basal subset—the Krt23+ activated basal cells—that are uniquely susceptible to RSV, expanding the known cellular tropism of RSV. Infection of basal cells can impact airway differentiation, homeostasis, and remodeling. Overall, our findings expand on RSV pathogenesis and indicate there are alternative mechanisms of infection and cell populations that are susceptible to RSV.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 每年在幼儿、老年人和免疫功能低下人群中引起数百万例下呼吸道感染 (LRTI)。RSV 感染始于上呼吸道,可进展至下呼吸道,导致 毛细支气管炎、肺炎,甚至死亡。RSV 主要感染顶部上皮细胞,但我们假设呼吸道上皮的基底外侧暴露可能提供另一种感染机制,有助于 LRTI 的发展。使用人鼻类器官-空气-液体界面 (HNO-ALI) 模型,我们对同时代的 RSV 毒株(RSV/A/安大略 [RSV/A/ON] 和 RSV/B/布宜诺斯艾利斯 [RSV/B/BA])进行顶端和基底外侧接种,代表成人和婴儿来源的 HNO-ALI 中的两个 RSV 亚群(A 和 B)。与顶端感染相比,基底外侧 RSV 暴露导致病毒复制和顶端释放延迟。RSV/B/BA 和 RSV/A/ON 之间的基底外侧感染频率存在统计学显着差异(81.3% 对比 25%)。基底外侧感染选择性地针对罕见的基底细胞群,同时保持上皮完整性。使用未分化的 HNO-ALI,我们首次确定 Krt23+ 激活的基底细胞对 RSV 感染特别敏感,我们在完全分化的 HNO-ALI 中证实了这一发现。总之,我们的研究结果表明,RSV 可以通过最初针对罕见的基底细胞亚群,然后向顶部传播到纤毛细胞,从基底外侧感染呼吸道上皮。此外,RSV/B/BA在利用基底外侧感染途径方面可能比RSV/A/ON具有优势。这些发现强调了 RSV 感染的另一种途径,并且可能是 RSV 传播到下呼吸道的潜在机制。重要性 了解 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 的 发病机制 对于了解和预防感染引起的急性和长期后遗症至关重要。对 RSV 感染的典型理解是,病毒在吸入或接触污染物后会感染并仅限于顶端纤毛细胞。我们证明 RSV 可以利用另一种感染途径(基底外侧途径)来感染呼吸道上皮的顶端纤毛细胞。我们还首次展示了两种同时期 RSV 毒株(RSV/A/安大略省和 RSV/B/布宜诺斯艾利斯)之间感染性的新差异。此外,我们描述了一种罕见的基底亚群——Krt23+激活的基底细胞——它们对RSV特别敏感,扩展了RSV已知的细胞趋向性。基底细胞的感染会影响气道分化、稳态和重塑。总体而言,我们的研究结果扩展了 RSV 发病机制,并表明存在对 RSV 敏感的替代感染机制和细胞群。

papers.full_text: Abstract Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) impairs STAT3 activation in infected ciliated cells in infants, but not adults, causing apoptosis to facilitate virus spread. How age regulates the STAT3 response to RSV in human bronchial epithelial cells (BEpiCs) is unknown. Here, we identify an age-associated immune-poised physiological state in human bronchial basal stem cells (BSCs) and progeny BEpiCs, rendering robust RIG-I to guard against the inactivation of RIG-I-STAT3 signaling by RSV nonstructural protein 2. In contrast, infant BEpiCs are vulnerable to such inactivation by RSV due to lower RIG-I levels. We show that acute respiratory viral infection in specific pathogen-free mice, rather than physical age, triggers sustained epigenetic and transcriptomic remodeling in BEpiCs that resembles age-associated changes in human BEpiCs. In addition, cytokine pretreatment of human neonatal BSCs induces an adult-like immune-poised state that is maintained in progeny BEpiCs to defend against RSV. Therefore, respiratory infection and inflammation during a lifetime imparts the effect of age to BSCs, which fortifies RIG-I in progeny cells to mitigate RSV infection. papers.title_original: An immune-poised state of human bronchial epithelial cells mediates defense against RSV in adults

analysis.research_question_and_background: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) impairs STAT3 activation in infected ciliated cells in infants but not adults, yet the mechanism by which age regulates the STAT3 response to RSV in human bronchial epithelial cells (BEpiCs) remains unknown.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study investigated age-associated immune-poised states in human bronchial basal stem cells (BSCs) and their progeny BEpiCs, comparing infant and adult cells, and used specific pathogen-free mice to model acute respiratory viral infection.
analysis.methods: The authors examined RIG-I levels and RIG-I-STAT3 signaling in human BSCs and BEpiCs, assessed epigenetic and transcriptomic remodeling in mouse BEpiCs following viral infection, and evaluated cytokine pretreatment effects on neonatal BSCs to induce adult-like states.
analysis.main_results: RSV nonstructural protein 2 inactivates RIG-I-STAT3 signaling in infant BEpiCs due to lower RIG-I levels, whereas adult BEpiCs maintain robust RIG-I signaling and resist inactivation, and acute viral infection in mice triggers sustained epigenetic and transcriptomic changes in BEpiCs resembling human age-associated states.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings reveal that prior respiratory infections and inflammation epigenetically program basal stem cells to fortify RIG-I in progeny BEpiCs, mitigating RSV infection, and demonstrate that cytokine pretreatment can induce an adult-like immune-poised state in neonatal cells.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This work suggests that interventions targeting basal stem cell programming or RIG-I induction could enhance RSV resistance, particularly in infants, and highlights the role of early-life infections in shaping lifelong epithelial antiviral defenses.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on in vitro human cell models and mouse infection data, limiting direct translation to human infants, and does not address long-term durability or potential off-target effects of cytokine-induced immune-poised states, warranting cautious interpretation.

analysis.summary_en: This study addresses why RSV causes severe disease in infants but not adults by investigating age-related differences in bronchial epithelial cell responses. The authors demonstrate that adult bronchial basal stem cells and their progeny epithelial cells maintain robust RIG-I-STAT3 signaling that resists inactivation by RSV nonstructural protein 2, whereas infant cells are vulnerable due to lower RIG-I levels. Using mouse models, they show that acute respiratory viral infection triggers epigenetic and transcriptomic changes in epithelial cells that mimic adult-like states, and cytokine pretreatment can induce these protective states in neonatal cells. The findings reveal a lifelong imprinting mechanism where prior infections program basal stem cells to fortify antiviral defenses in progeny cells, offering potential avenues for therapeutic intervention to enhance RSV resistance in infants.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 会损害婴儿而非成人受感染纤毛细胞中 STAT3 的激活,但年龄调节人支气管上皮细胞 (BEpiC) 中 STAT3 对 RSV 反应的机制仍不清楚。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究调查了人类支气管基底干细胞 (BSC) 及其后代 BEpiC 中与年龄相关的免疫平衡状态,比较了婴儿和成人细胞,并使用特定的无病原体小鼠来模拟急性呼吸道病毒感染。
elements_zh.methods: 作者检查了人类 BSC 和 BEpiC 中的 RIG-I 水平和 RIG-I-STAT3 信号传导,评估了病毒感染后小鼠 BEpiC 中的表观遗传和转录组重塑,并评估了细胞因子预处理对新生儿 BSC 诱导成人样状态的影响。
elements_zh.main_results: 由于 RIG-I 水平较低,RSV 非结构蛋白 2 使婴​​儿 BEpiC 中的 RIG-I-STAT3 信号失活,而成人 BEpiC 则保持强大的 RIG-I 信号并抵抗失活,小鼠的急性病毒感染会触发 BEpiC 中持续的表观遗传和转录组变化,类似于人类年龄相关状态。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,先前的呼吸道感染和炎症对基底干细胞进行表观遗传编程,以增强后代 BEpiC 中的 RIG-I,从而减轻 RSV 感染,并证明细胞因子预处理可以在新生儿细胞中诱导类似成人的免疫平衡状态。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这项工作表明,针对基础干细胞编程或 RIG-I 诱导的干预措施可以增强 RSV 抵抗力,特别是在婴儿中,并强调了生命早期感染在塑造终生上皮 抗病毒药物 防御中的作用。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究依赖于体外人类细胞模型和小鼠感染数据,限制了对人类婴儿的直接转化,并且没有解决细胞因子诱导的免疫平衡状态的长期持久性或潜在的脱靶效应,需要谨慎解释。

papers.title: Changes in the pathogenic characteristics of hospitalized children with community-acquired pneumonia in Changzhou, China, 2018-2023.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) is a significant cause of hospitalization and mortality in children. Non-pharmacological interventions (NPIs) implemented during the COVID-19 pandemic were associated with changes in the transmission dynamics of respiratory pathogens. The present study aimed to analyze changes in the pathogenic characteristics of hospitalized children with CAP in a single-center pediatric cohort in Changzhou, China, before and after the outbreak of COVID-19. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed demographic information, hospitalization records, and pathogen-detection results of children admitted for CAP at Changzhou Children's Hospital, Jiangsu Province, China, from 2018 to 2023. The analyzed pathogens included eight target bacteria and seven respiratory viruses. RESULTS: A total of 29,552 children hospitalized with CAP were included, including 15,124 in the pre-pandemic period, 9024 in the pandemic period, and 5404 in the post-pandemic period. The male-to-female ratio was 1.42:1, and the median age was 16 months (IQR: 5.0-37.0). Hospitalizations generally peaked in autumn and winter from 2018 to 2022, whereas an off-season peak occurred in May 2023. The overall bacterial positivity increased from 9.94% before the pandemic to 13.96% during the pandemic and 13.68% after the pandemic, while viral positivity increased from 16.52% to 21.43% and 21.06%, respectively. In contrast, coinfection positivity decreased from 6.89% before the pandemic to 5.13% during the pandemic and 3.02% after the pandemic. Across all three periods, Escherichia coli consistently ranked first among bacterial detections, while RSV remained the predominant virus among viral detections. CONCLUSIONS: Noticeable shifts in the detection spectrum and positivity rates of common bacterial and viral pathogens were observed among hospitalized children with CAP following the implementation and relaxation of COVID-19 prevention and control policies. Continuous long-term surveillance is needed to refine targeted prevention strategies and optimize clinical treatment protocols for pediatric CAP. CLINICAL TRIAL: Not applicable.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines changes in the pathogenic characteristics of hospitalized children with community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) in Changzhou, China, from 2018 to 2023, focusing on the impact of non-pharmacological interventions (NPIs) during and after the COVID-19 pandemic on pathogen detection patterns and transmission dynamics in pediatric CAP.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a retrospective single-center study analyzing demographic information, hospitalization records, and pathogen-detection results of 29,552 children admitted for CAP at Changzhou Children's Hospital, including 15,124 in the pre-pandemic period, 9,024 during the pandemic, and 5,404 in the post-pandemic period. The study reviewed eight target bacteria and seven respiratory viruses.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review reports a consistent increase in bacterial and viral positivity rates among hospitalized children with CAP across the three periods: bacterial positivity rose from 9.94% pre-pandemic to 13.96% during the pandemic and 13.68% post-pandemic, while viral positivity increased from 16.52% to 21.43% and 21.06%, respectively. Coinfection positivity decreased from 6.89% pre-pandemic to 5.13% during the pandemic and 3.02% post-pandemic. Escherichia coli and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) remained the most frequently detected bacterial and viral pathogens, respectively.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review does not report the specific mechanisms underlying the observed shifts in pathogen detection patterns or the long-term clinical implications of these changes. Additionally, the single-center design and retrospective nature limit generalizability, and the study does not address potential confounding factors such as vaccination coverage or local policy variations.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review highlights the need for continuous long-term surveillance to refine targeted prevention strategies and optimize clinical treatment protocols for pediatric CAP, particularly in light of the observed shifts in pathogen detection patterns following the implementation and relaxation of COVID-19 prevention and control policies.

analysis.summary_en: This review analyzes changes in the pathogenic characteristics of hospitalized children with community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) in Changzhou, China, from 2018 to 2023, focusing on the impact of non-pharmacological interventions (NPIs) during and after the COVID-19 pandemic. Escherichia coli and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) remained the most frequently detected pathogens. The review underscores the need for ongoing surveillance to adapt prevention and treatment strategies for pediatric CAP in response to evolving pathogen dynamics.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述研究了 2018 年至 2023 年中国常州社区获得性肺炎 (CAP) 住院儿童病原学特征的变化,重点关注 COVID-19 大流行期间和之后非药物干预 (NPI) 对儿科 CAP 病原检测模式和 传播 动态的影响。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该评价是一项回顾性单中心研究,分析了常州儿童医院收治的 29,552 名 CAP 儿童的人口统计信息、住院记录和病原体检测结果,其中疫情前 15,124 名,疫情期间 9,024 名,疫情后 5,404 名。该研究回顾了八种目标细菌和七种呼吸道病毒。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该综述报告说,三个时期内CAP住院儿童的细菌和病毒阳性率持续上升:细菌阳性率从大流行前的9.94%上升到大流行期间的13.96%和大流行后的13.68%,而病毒阳性率分别从16.52%上升到21.43%和21.06%。混合感染阳性率从大流行前的 6.89% 下降至大流行期间的 5.13% 和大流行后的 3.02%。大肠杆菌和 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 仍然分别是最常检测到的细菌和病毒病原体。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述没有报告观察到的病原体检测模式变化的具体机制或这些变化的长期临床影响。此外,单中心设计和回顾性限制了普遍性,并且该研究没有解决潜在的混杂因素,例如 疫苗接种 覆盖范围或当地政策变化。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该审查强调需要持续长期的 监测 来完善有针对性的预防策略并优化儿科 CAP 的临床 治疗 方案,特别是考虑到在实施和放松 COVID-19 预防和控制政策后观察到的病原体检测模式的变化。

papers.title: How Pandemics Have Reshaped the Respiratory Virus Data Landscape in Europe: Scoping Review
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Acute respiratory infections caused by influenza, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and SARS-CoV-2 remain a major public health challenge in Europe. Although surveillance systems for these pathogens are well established, the past 2 decades have seen a rapid diversification of data streams supporting surveillance and research. This expanding data landscape, combined with fragmentation across institutions, sectors, and countries, may limit timely evidence synthesis and effective public health decision-making. Objective This scoping review aimed to identify and characterize data sources used for surveillance and research on influenza, RSV, and SARS-CoV-2 in Europe over the past 20 years, and to examine their evolution over time, their alignment with research objectives, and geographic variation in data availability and use. Methods We conducted a scoping review using an objective-driven analytical framework. Empirical reports published between January 2005 and September 2025 were identified in MEDLINE, Web of Science, and Embase. elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述审查了过去 20 年来欧洲 监测 的数据源以及流感、呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 和 SARS-CoV-2 的研究,重点关注 进化、与研究目标的一致性以及 12 个欧洲国家之间可用性和使用的地理差异。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 使用目标驱动的分析框架进行了范围界定审查,确定了 2005 年 1 月至 2025 年 9 月在 MEDLINE、Web of Science 和 Embase 上发表的实证报告。符合条件的报告重点关注流感、RSV 或 SARS-CoV-2,包括来自 12 个欧洲国家的数据,不包括临床和干预研究。

elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 加强准备工作需要可互操作的基础设施、联合分析平台、对 监测 创新的可持续资助以及跨部门数据共享,以解决地理差异并改善整个欧洲的综合数据使用。

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 由流感、呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 和 SARS-CoV-2 引起的急性呼吸道感染仍然是欧洲的主要公共卫生挑战。尽管针对这些病原体的 监测 系统已经很完善,但在过去 20 年中,支持 监测 和研究的数据流迅速多样化。这种不断扩大的数据格局,加上机构、部门和国家之间的碎片化,可能会限制及时的证据综合和有效的公共卫生决策。目的 本次范围界定审查旨在确定和描述过去 20 年来欧洲用于 监测 以及流感、RSV 和 SARS-CoV-2 研究的数据源,并检查其 进化 随着时间的推移、其与研究目标的一致性以及数据可用性和使用的地理差异。方法 我们使用目标驱动的分析框架进行了范围界定审查。MEDLINE、Web of Science 和 Embase 确定了 2005 年 1 月至 2025 年 9 月期间发表的实证报告。符合条件的报告重点关注流感、RSV 或 SARS-CoV-2,并包含来自 12 个欧洲国家的数据。临床和介入研究被排除在外。报告根据 4 个研究目标进行分类:流行病学监测、干预措施评估、疾病负担和健康结果评估,以及人口对公共卫生措施的依从性和信任度分析。数据源分为 9 类,包括 监测 系统、电子健康记录 (EHR)、登记、索赔、调查、数字、环境、综合数据集等。结果共纳入2564份实证报告。随着时间的推移,呼吸道病毒研究依赖于越来越多样化的数据流。虽然 监测 系统仍然处于核心地位,特别是在流行病学监测方面,但其相对主导地位有所下降。从 2020 年起,电子病历、登记、索赔数据、数字源以及链接或集成数据集的使用显着扩大,同时开放获取数据的使用也有所增加。数据源用途因研究目标而异:监测 数据在监测和干预评估中占主导地位;风险因素和 治疗 有效性研究中的 EHR;血清流行率 调查和公众信任分析;以及经济负担评估中的索赔数据。观察到了巨大的地理差异。北欧国家更频繁地使用链接和多源数据集,而南欧国家更频繁地依赖开放访问或单一来源数据。结论 本次范围界定审查应用创新的目标驱动框架,为呼吸道病毒 监测 和欧洲 20 年来的研究提供了多病原体、跨国数据源图谱。与之前专注于单一病原体或数据类型的审查不同,它提供了基于 2564 份报告的综合比较视角,为公共卫生决策提供信息。COVID-19 大流行加速了数据生成和获取方面的创新,但进展仍然主要集中在 SARS-CoV-2 上,而结构碎片化继续限制整个欧洲及时、整合的数据。加强准备工作需要可互操作的基础设施、联合分析平台、监测 创新的可持续资金以及跨部门数据共享。

papers.title: Bridging the Vaccine Gap: Scientific and Technological Advances for Diseases Lacking Effective Vaccines.
papers.abstract: Despite remarkable achievements in infectious disease control, more than 20 major pathogens responsible for significant global morbidity and mortality remain without licensed, effective vaccines. This so-called 'vaccine gap' disproportionately burdens low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), exacerbating health inequities and threatening global pandemic preparedness. This review comprehensively examines scientific and technological advances that are actively bridging the vaccine gap, with emphasis on novel platform technologies, immunological innovations, and translational strategies. We conducted a systematic narrative review of literature published between 2015 and 2024, encompassing peer-reviewed articles, WHO reports, clinical trial registries, and regulatory agency databases. Six transformative technology clusters were identified: (1) mRNA and self-amplifying RNA (saRNA) platforms enabling rapid antigen production; (2) viral-vectored vaccines with improved immune breadth; (3) structure-guided antigen design using cryo-electron microscopy and artificial intelligence (AI)-driven protein engineering; (4) broadly neutralising monoclonal antibodies as surrogate vaccine benchmarks; (5) mucosal and inhalable delivery systems targeting tissue-resident immunity; and (6) combination adjuvant systems amplifying magnitude and durability of protective responses. Clinical translation is exemplified by candidates against HIV-1, tuberculosis (TB), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in infants, and Plasmodium falciparum malaria. Convergence of AI-assisted rational antigen design, next-generation mRNA platforms, and innovative adjuvant-delivery pairings represents a paradigm shift toward vaccinatable diseases previously considered intractable. Equitable access frameworks and regulatory harmonisation across LMICs remain critical unresolved challenges.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review addresses pathogens without licensed effective vaccines, focusing on diseases causing significant global morbidity and mortality, with emphasis on low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) and the central question of bridging the 'vaccine gap' through scientific and technological advances.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A systematic narrative review was conducted covering literature from 2015 to 2024, including peer-reviewed articles, WHO reports, clinical trial registries, and regulatory agency databases, though the exact number of included studies is not reported.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Six transformative vaccine technology clusters were identified: mRNA and self-amplifying RNA platforms, viral-vectored vaccines, structure-guided antigen design using cryo-electron microscopy and AI, broadly neutralising monoclonal antibodies, mucosal and inhalable delivery systems, and combination adjuvant systems, with clinical translation exemplified in HIV-1, tuberculosis, RSV in infants, and Plasmodium falciparum malaria.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Equitable access frameworks and regulatory harmonisation across LMICs remain critical unresolved challenges, indicating gaps in policy implementation and global health equity despite technological advances.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The convergence of AI-assisted antigen design, next-generation mRNA platforms, and innovative adjuvant-delivery pairings signals a paradigm shift toward vaccinatable diseases previously considered intractable, necessitating targeted research and policy alignment.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines the persistent 'vaccine gap' for over 20 major pathogens causing significant global morbidity and mortality, particularly affecting LMICs. It systematically evaluates advances from 2015 to 2024, identifying six transformative vaccine technology clusters: mRNA and self-amplifying RNA platforms, viral-vectored vaccines, AI-driven antigen design, broadly neutralising antibodies, mucosal delivery systems, and combination adjuvants. Clinical translation is highlighted in HIV-1, tuberculosis, RSV in infants, and malaria. However, equitable access and regulatory harmonisation across LMICs remain unresolved challenges. The convergence of AI, next-generation mRNA platforms, and innovative adjuvants signals a paradigm shift toward tackling previously intractable diseases.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该审查针对未经许可的有效 疫苗 病原体,重点关注导致全球重大发病率的疾病和 疫苗,重点关注低收入和中等收入国家 (LMIC) 以及通过科技进步弥合“疫苗 差距”的核心问题。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 对 2015 年至 2024 年的文献进行了系统的叙述性综述,包括同行评审的文章、世界卫生组织报告、临床试验登记处和监管机构数据库,但未报告纳入研究的确切数量。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 确定了六个变革性的 疫苗 技术集群:mRNA 和自扩增 RNA 平台、病毒载体 疫苗、使用冷冻电子显微镜和人工智能的结构引导抗原设计、广泛中和单克隆抗体、粘膜和可吸入递送系统以及组合佐剂系统,临床转化以 HIV-1、结核病、婴儿 RSV 和恶性疟原虫为例疟疾。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 中低收入国家的公平获取框架和监管协调仍然是尚未解决的重大挑战,这表明尽管技术取得了进步,但政策实施和全球卫生公平方面仍存在差距。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 人工智能辅助抗原设计、下一代 mRNA 平台和创新佐剂递送配对的融合标志着向以前被认为是棘手的疫苗疾病的范式转变,需要有针对性的研究和政策调整。

papers.title: From triplex to tetraplex: evaluation of the diagnostic accuracy of the new Roche Cobas Liat SARS-CoV-2, influenza A/B & RSV assay
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Rapid and accurate diagnostics of epidemic respiratory viruses are relevant for optimal care pathways. In this observational diagnostic accuracy study, the novel Cobas Liat assay (Roche Molecular Systems) was evaluated for the detection of SARS-CoV-2, influenza A and B, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in the clinical setting of Tampere University Hospital, Tampere, Finland. In addition, the added value of the tetraplex assay instead of two partially overlapping triplex assays (influenza A/B and SARS-CoV-2 or RSV) was assessed in the context of adult and pediatric emergency department (AED, PED) point-of-care (PoC) testing environments. A total of 315 clinical nasopharyngeal swab samples were analyzed. Diagnostic accuracy was evaluated against a molecular diagnostic reference. The evaluated Cobas Liat assay had sensitivities and specificities of 100% and 98.5% for influenza A, 100% and 99.7% for influenza B, 100% and 98.2% for SARS-CoV-2, and 100% and 97.0% for RSV, respectively. Among the index and reference tests, the Cobas Liat assay demonstrated the highest analytical sensitivity for influenza A, SARS-CoV-2, and RSV. No cross-reactivity with off-panel microbes was observed. With respect to clinical applicability, implementation of the evaluated tetraplex test would decrease double testing with two triplex tests in PED, likely decreasing costs and hands-on work. In AED, tetraplex testing would likely significantly increase the diagnostic yield for RSV, only rarely covered by PoC testing in AED. The evaluated Cobas Liat assay had excellent clinical and analytical accuracy, being highly suitable for PoC use but also for laboratory-based testing of influenza viruses, SARS-CoV-2, and RSV. IMPORTANCE Until recently, rapid point-of-care diagnostics have been somewhat limited by triplex four-channel analysis technology, separating four of the most important epidemic respiratory viruses—influenza A, influenza B, respiratory syncytial virus, and SARS-CoV-2—into two individual triplex tests. The evaluated tetraplex respiratory viral assay combines the two partially overlapping tests into a single test, streamlining analysis in two-test settings and potentially reducing diagnostic gaps in one-test settings. To our knowledge, this is the first study to describe the diagnostic accuracy of the novel Cobas Liat SARS-CoV-2, influenza A/B, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) assay with additional considerations for analytical sensitivity and specificity, and clinical utility in adult and pediatric emergency department use.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Rapid and accurate diagnostics for epidemic respiratory viruses are critical for optimal care pathways, but rapid point-of-care testing has been limited by triplex technology that separates key viruses into overlapping assays. The study addressed the need for a single tetraplex assay to streamline testing and reduce diagnostic gaps.
analysis.study_design_and_population: An observational diagnostic accuracy study evaluated the novel Cobas Liat tetraplex assay (Roche Molecular Systems) for detecting SARS-CoV-2, influenza A/B, and RSV in Tampere University Hospital, Finland. A total of 315 clinical nasopharyngeal swab samples were analyzed in adult and pediatric emergency department point-of-care settings.
analysis.methods: Diagnostic accuracy was assessed against a molecular diagnostic reference. The study evaluated the added value of the tetraplex assay compared to two partially overlapping triplex assays in point-of-care testing environments. Analytical sensitivity and specificity were determined for each virus.
analysis.main_results: The Cobas Liat assay demonstrated sensitivities and specificities of 100% and 98.5% for influenza A, 100% and 99.7% for influenza B, 100% and 98.2% for SARS-CoV-2, and 100% and 97.0% for RSV, respectively. No cross-reactivity with off-panel microbes was observed.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The tetraplex assay showed excellent clinical and analytical accuracy, being highly suitable for point-of-care and laboratory-based testing. To the authors' knowledge, this is the first study to describe the diagnostic accuracy of the novel Cobas Liat SARS-CoV-2, influenza A/B, and RSV assay with considerations for analytical sensitivity, specificity, and clinical utility in emergency department settings.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Implementation of the tetraplex test would decrease double testing with two triplex tests in pediatric emergency departments, likely reducing costs and hands-on work. In adult emergency departments, tetraplex testing would likely increase the diagnostic yield for RSV, which is rarely covered by point-of-care testing.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was conducted in a single hospital setting with a limited sample size of 315 nasopharyngeal swabs, which may affect generalisability. The evidence is derived from an observational diagnostic accuracy study without randomization, limiting causal inference.

analysis.summary_en: This observational diagnostic accuracy study evaluated the novel Roche Cobas Liat tetraplex assay for detecting SARS-CoV-2, influenza A/B, and RSV in Tampere University Hospital, Finland. The assay demonstrated perfect sensitivity (100%) and high specificity (97.0%–99.7%) for all viruses tested, with no cross-reactivity observed. The tetraplex format streamlines testing by combining two overlapping triplex assays into a single test, reducing double testing and hands-on work in pediatric emergency departments and increasing RSV diagnostic yield in adult emergency departments. The study is the first to assess the assay's diagnostic accuracy and clinical utility in emergency department point-of-care settings, highlighting its potential for improving respiratory virus diagnostics.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 流行性呼吸道病毒的快速、准确诊断对于最佳护理途径至关重要,但快速护理点检测受到三重技术的限制,该技术将关键病毒分离到重叠的检测中。该研究解决了对单一四重检测的需求,以简化测试并减少诊断差距。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 一项观察性诊断准确性研究评估了芬兰坦佩雷大学医院用于检测 SARS-CoV-2、甲型/乙型流感和 RSV 的新型 Cobas Liat 四联检测(罗氏分子系统)。在成人和儿童急诊科护理点环境中对总共 315 份临床鼻咽拭子样本进行了分析。
elements_zh.methods: 根据分子诊断参考评估诊断准确性。该研究评估了四重检测与在护理点测试环境中两个部分重叠的三重检测相比的附加价值。确定了每种病毒的分析灵敏度和特异性。
elements_zh.main_results: Cobas Liat 检测显示,甲型流感的敏感性和特异性分别为 100% 和 98.5%,乙型流感为 100% 和 99.7%,SARS-CoV-2 为 100% 和 98.2%,RSV 为 100% 和 97.0%。未观察到与面板外微生物的交叉反应。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 四重检测显示出出色的临床和分析准确性,非常适合现场护理和实验室测试。据作者所知,这是第一项描述新型 Cobas Liat SARS-CoV-2、甲型/乙型流感和 RSV 检测的诊断准确性的研究,同时考虑了分析灵敏度、特异性和在急诊科环境中的临床实用性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 四重测试的实施将减少儿科急诊科中两次三重测试的双重测试,可能会降低成本和实际工作。在成人急诊科,四重检测可能会提高 RSV 的诊断率,而护理点检测很少涵盖 RSV。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是在一家医院环境中进行的,样本量有限,只有 315 份鼻咽拭子,这可能会影响普适性。证据来自观察性诊断准确性研究,没有随机化,限制了因果推断。

analysis_zh.methods: 根据分子诊断参考评估诊断准确性。该研究评估了四重检测与在护理点测试环境中两个部分重叠的三重检测相比的附加价值。确定了每种病毒的分析灵敏度和特异性。
analysis_zh.main_results: Cobas Liat 检测显示,甲型流感的敏感性和特异性分别为 100% 和 98.5%,乙型流感为 100% 和 99.7%,SARS-CoV-2 为 100% 和 98.2%,RSV 为 100% 和 97.0%。未观察到与面板外微生物的交叉反应。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 四重检测显示出出色的临床和分析准确性,非常适合现场护理和实验室测试。据作者所知,这是第一项描述新型 Cobas Liat SARS-CoV-2、甲型/乙型流感和 RSV 检测的诊断准确性的研究,同时考虑了分析灵敏度、特异性和在急诊科环境中的临床实用性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 四重测试的实施将减少儿科急诊科中两次三重测试的双重测试,可能会降低成本和实际工作。在成人急诊科,四重检测可能会提高 RSV 的诊断率,而护理点检测很少涵盖 RSV。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是在一家医院环境中进行的,样本量有限,只有 315 份鼻咽拭子,这可能会影响普适性。证据来自观察性诊断准确性研究,没有随机化,限制了因果推断。

papers.title: CAUSAL-RSV: Causal Analysis of RSV Vaccine Effects in Infants Using Real-World Data
papers.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) contributes to substantial morbidity and mortality in young children each year. In 2023, two new prevention products were licensed and recommended in the United States (US), including a prefusion F protein subunit vaccine (RSVpreF) administered during pregnancy and a long-acting monoclonal antibody (mAb) administered in infants. Although post-licensure real-world studies support the effectiveness of RSVpreF vaccine during pregnancy, existing studies have been conducted in settings where only RSVpreF vaccine is available. The real-world effectiveness of RSVpreF vaccine in settings where both RSVpreF vaccine and mAbs are available is not yet well understood. The goal of this study is to estimate the real-world effectiveness of the RSVpreF vaccine against severe infant RSV by applying causal mediation analysis with receipt of mAbs as a mediating variable. Using a national cohort of mother-infant dyads with the Optum Labs Data Warehouse (OLDW), we will model vaccine and mAb effects in a longitudinal cohort spanning the 2023-24, 2024-25, and 2025-26 RSV seasons. Results will be used to better understand the total effect of RSVpreF vaccination when it is used as one component within a hybrid infant RSV prevention program.

papers.title_zh: CAUSAL-RSV:使用真实世界数据对 RSV 疫苗 对婴儿的影响进行因果分析
papers.source_body_en: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) contributes to substantial morbidity and mortality in young children each year. In 2023, two new prevention products were licensed and recommended in the United States (US), including a prefusion F protein subunit vaccine (RSVpreF) administered during pregnancy and a long-acting monoclonal antibody (mAb) administered in infants. Although post-licensure real-world studies support the effectiveness of RSVpreF vaccine during pregnancy, existing studies have been conducted in settings where only RSVpreF vaccine is available. The real-world effectiveness of RSVpreF vaccine in settings where both RSVpreF vaccine and mAbs are available is not yet well understood. The goal of this study is to estimate the real-world effectiveness of the RSVpreF vaccine against severe infant RSV by applying causal mediation analysis with receipt of mAbs as a mediating variable. Using a national cohort of mother-infant dyads with the Optum Labs Data Warehouse (OLDW), we will model vaccine and mAb effects in a longitudinal cohort spanning the 2023-24, 2024-25, and 2025-26 RSV seasons. Results will be used to better understand the total effect of RSVpreF vaccination when it is used as one component within a hybrid infant RSV prevention program.
papers.abstract_zh: 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 每年都会导致幼儿大量发病和 死亡率。2023年,两种新的预防产品在美国获得许可和推荐,包括在怀孕期间施用的预融合F蛋白亚基疫苗 (RSVpreF)和在婴儿中施用的长效单克隆抗体(mAb)。尽管获得许可后的真实世界研究支持 RSVpreF 疫苗 在怀孕期间的有效性,但现有研究是在仅提供 RSVpreF 疫苗 的环境中进行的。在 RSVpreF 疫苗 和 mAb 均可用的环境中,RSVpreF 疫苗 的实际有效性尚不清楚。本研究的目的是通过应用因果中介分析(以单克隆抗体接收作为中介变量)来估计 RSVpreF 疫苗 对严重婴儿 RSV 的实际有效性。使用 Optum Labs 数据仓库 (OLDW) 的全国母婴二元组 队列研究,我们将在跨越 2023-24、2024-25 和 2025-26 RSV 季节的纵向 队列研究 中对 疫苗 和 mAb 效应进行建模。当 RSVpreF 疫苗接种 用作混合婴儿 RSV 预防计划中的一个组成部分时,结果将用于更好地了解 RSVpreF 疫苗接种 的总体效果。

papers.title: RSV-associated hospitalizations among American Indian and Alaska Native children in Alaska and the Southwest United States, 2019-2023
papers.abstract: Abstract We conducted active surveillance for acute respiratory infection (ARI) among hospitalized AI/AN children ages <5 years at select health facilities in Alaska and the Southwest United States. Children in these communities continue to experience high rates of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV)-associated hospitalization, underscoring the need for prevention products.
papers.journal: Journal of the Pediatric Infectious Diseases Society

papers.title: Optimization of the antiviral spectrum of cyclophilin inhibitors targeting respiratory viruses.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT We evaluated the antiviral activity of a library of 36 urea-based small-molecule cyclophilin inhibitors (SMCypIs) against human respiratory syncytial virus (hRSV) and human metapneumovirus (hMPV). Structure–spectrum analysis revealed virus-specific structural requirements for antiviral efficacy. By combining the key determinants identified for each virus, we rationally designed optimized dual-acting derivatives. Among these, the optimized compound F832/33 emerged as a potent, broad-spectrum antiviral agent with nanomolar activity against both hRSV and hMPV, submicromolar inhibition of cyclophilin (Cyp) peptidyl-prolyl isomerase (PPIase) activity, and no detectable cytotoxicity. Interestingly, no direct correlation was observed between Cyp PPIase inhibition and antiviral potency, suggesting that Cyp engagement rather than enzymatic inhibition per se is required for antiviral activity. Competition assays with alisporivir confirmed that the antiviral effects of SMCypIs depend on their specific interaction with Cyp. Beyond its dual efficacy, F832/33 displayed strong antiviral activity against additional clinically relevant respiratory pathogens, including parainfluenza virus type 3, enterovirus D68, and both ancestral and Omicron severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 strains, in immortalized cell lines and fully differentiated human nasal epithelial cells, a physiologically relevant model of respiratory infection. Collectively, our results demonstrate that structure–activity relationship-guided optimization can be successfully applied to expand the antiviral spectrum of SMCypIs, positioning F832/33 as a promising host-targeted broad-spectrum antiviral candidate. Further in vivo studies are warranted to evaluate its therapeutic potential and clarify its precise mechanism of action.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the need for broad-spectrum antivirals against respiratory viruses with limited treatment options, specifically targeting human respiratory syncytial virus (hRSV) and human metapneumovirus (hMPV). The authors aimed to optimize cyclophilin inhibitors to expand their antiviral spectrum beyond existing narrow-spectrum activity.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study evaluated a library of 36 urea-based small-molecule cyclophilin inhibitors (SMCypIs) against hRSV and hMPV using structure–spectrum analysis and rational design. The optimized compound F832/33 was tested for antiviral activity, cyclophilin inhibition, and cytotoxicity in immortalized cell lines and fully differentiated human nasal epithelial cells.
analysis.methods: The authors performed structure–activity relationship-guided optimization to identify key determinants for antiviral efficacy against hRSV and hMPV. Antiviral potency was assessed using nanomolar and submicromolar inhibition assays, while cytotoxicity was evaluated. Competition assays with alisporivir were used to confirm the dependence of antiviral effects on cyclophilin interaction.
analysis.main_results: The optimized compound F832/33 demonstrated nanomolar activity against hRSV and hMPV, submicromolar inhibition of cyclophilin peptidyl-prolyl isomerase activity, and no detectable cytotoxicity. No direct correlation was observed between cyclophilin enzymatic inhibition and antiviral potency. F832/33 also showed strong antiviral activity against parainfluenza virus type 3, enterovirus D68, and both ancestral and Omicron SARS-CoV-2 strains in cell models.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings indicate that cyclophilin engagement, rather than enzymatic inhibition, is critical for antiviral activity, highlighting a novel mechanism for broad-spectrum antiviral development. The study demonstrates that rational design can successfully expand the antiviral spectrum of SMCypIs, positioning F832/33 as a promising host-targeted candidate.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results suggest that F832/33 could serve as a broad-spectrum antiviral for multiple respiratory pathogens, addressing unmet needs in treatment options. The host-targeted mechanism may reduce resistance development and provide a platform for optimizing antivirals against emerging respiratory viruses.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to in vitro and cell-based models, with no in vivo data provided. The study relies on abstract-level evidence, and further preclinical and clinical evaluations are needed to confirm therapeutic potential and mechanism of action.

analysis.summary_en: This study optimized urea-based small-molecule cyclophilin inhibitors (SMCypIs) to broaden their antiviral spectrum against respiratory viruses. By evaluating 36 compounds against human respiratory syncytial virus (hRSV) and human metapneumovirus (hMPV), the authors identified structural requirements for antiviral efficacy and rationally designed the dual-acting derivative F832/33. The compound exhibited nanomolar antiviral activity against hRSV and hMPV, submicromolar cyclophilin inhibition, and no cytotoxicity, while also demonstrating activity against parainfluenza virus type 3, enterovirus D68, and SARS-CoV-2 variants. Mechanistic studies suggested that cyclophilin engagement, rather than enzymatic inhibition, drives antiviral effects. The findings highlight a novel host-targeted approach for broad-spectrum antivirals, though further in vivo studies are required to validate therapeutic potential.

papers.title_zh: 针对呼吸道病毒的亲环蛋白抑制剂 抗病毒药物 谱的优化。
papers.source_body_en: ABSTRACT We evaluated the antiviral activity of a library of 36 urea-based small-molecule cyclophilin inhibitors (SMCypIs) against human respiratory syncytial virus (hRSV) and human metapneumovirus (hMPV). Structure–spectrum analysis revealed virus-specific structural requirements for antiviral efficacy. By combining the key determinants identified for each virus, we rationally designed optimized dual-acting derivatives. Among these, the optimized compound F832/33 emerged as a potent, broad-spectrum antiviral agent with nanomolar activity against both hRSV and hMPV, submicromolar inhibition of cyclophilin (Cyp) peptidyl-prolyl isomerase (PPIase) activity, and no detectable cytotoxicity. Interestingly, no direct correlation was observed between Cyp PPIase inhibition and antiviral potency, suggesting that Cyp engagement rather than enzymatic inhibition per se is required for antiviral activity. Competition assays with alisporivir confirmed that the antiviral effects of SMCypIs depend on their specific interaction with Cyp. Beyond its dual efficacy, F832/33 displayed strong antiviral activity against additional clinically relevant respiratory pathogens, including parainfluenza virus type 3, enterovirus D68, and both ancestral and Omicron severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 strains, in immortalized cell lines and fully differentiated human nasal epithelial cells, a physiologically relevant model of respiratory infection. Collectively, our results demonstrate that structure–activity relationship-guided optimization can be successfully applied to expand the antiviral spectrum of SMCypIs, positioning F832/33 as a promising host-targeted broad-spectrum antiviral candidate. Further in vivo studies are warranted to evaluate its therapeutic potential and clarify its precise mechanism of action.

papers.title: Age-Dependent Differences in the Antiviral Response of the Respiratory Epithelium
papers.abstract: Age is an established risk factor for severe viral respiratory infections, yet the mechanisms driving increased severity of illness in infants and older adults remain incompletely understood. The respiratory epithelium is the primary target of viral infection and how it orchestrates the immune response may be a key determinant of clinical outcomes. The profound age-related difference in susceptibility to severe Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) brought increased attention to the epithelial response to viral infection in children and adults, adding significant data to the preexisting body of work largely focused on influenza and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). This review synthesizes current knowledge on the structural and functional differences in the respiratory epithelium between children and adults at baseline and during viral infection. We review the variable and heterogenous human studies in addition to in vitro and animal model data to identify key gaps in current knowledge. Here, we advocate for a more complete understanding of age-dependent differences in the respiratory epithelial response to viral infection to uncover therapeutic targets for prevention and treatment of viral-associated respiratory failure.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines age-dependent differences in the antiviral response of the respiratory epithelium, focusing on the pathogen-agnostic mechanisms underlying severe viral respiratory infections across infants, children, and older adults. The central question addresses how structural and functional variations in the respiratory epithelium between age groups influence clinical outcomes during viral infection.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review synthesizes heterogeneous human studies, in vitro experiments, and animal model data to compare baseline and infection-induced epithelial responses across age groups. It integrates preexisting knowledge on influenza and RSV with emerging data on COVID-19 to identify mechanistic gaps.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Age is a well-established risk factor for severe viral respiratory infections, with the respiratory epithelium serving as the primary site of viral infection and immune orchestration. The review highlights that the increased susceptibility to severe COVID-19 in specific age groups has intensified focus on epithelial responses, expanding beyond traditional pathogens like influenza and RSV.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The mechanisms driving increased severity of illness in infants and older adults remain incompletely understood, despite age being a recognized risk factor. Current knowledge is limited by variable and heterogeneous study designs, with a lack of mechanistic clarity on how epithelial responses differ across age groups during viral infection.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: A deeper understanding of age-dependent epithelial responses is needed to uncover therapeutic targets for preventing and treating viral-associated respiratory failure. The review advocates for targeted research to address these gaps, particularly in elucidating the molecular and cellular pathways that contribute to severe outcomes in vulnerable age groups.

analysis.summary_en: This review investigates how age-dependent differences in the respiratory epithelium influence antiviral responses and clinical outcomes during viral respiratory infections. It synthesizes heterogeneous human, in vitro, and animal data, emphasizing that age is a critical risk factor for severe disease. While the respiratory epithelium is central to infection and immune regulation, the mechanisms underlying increased severity in infants and older adults remain poorly understood. The review highlights gaps in mechanistic knowledge and calls for targeted research to identify therapeutic targets for preventing viral-associated respiratory failure.

elements_en.scope_and_question: The review examines age-dependent differences in the antiviral response of the respiratory epithelium, focusing on the pathogen-agnostic mechanisms underlying severe viral respiratory infections across infants, children, and older adults. The central question addresses how structural and functional variations in the respiratory epithelium between age groups influence clinical outcomes during viral infection.
elements_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review synthesizes heterogeneous human studies, in vitro experiments, and animal model data to compare baseline and infection-induced epithelial responses across age groups. It integrates preexisting knowledge on influenza and RSV with emerging data on COVID-19 to identify mechanistic gaps.
elements_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Age is a well-established risk factor for severe viral respiratory infections, with the respiratory epithelium serving as the primary site of viral infection and immune orchestration. The review highlights that the increased susceptibility to severe COVID-19 in specific age groups has intensified focus on epithelial responses, expanding beyond traditional pathogens like influenza and RSV.
elements_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The mechanisms driving increased severity of illness in infants and older adults remain incompletely understood, despite age being a recognized risk factor. Current knowledge is limited by variable and heterogeneous study designs, with a lack of mechanistic clarity on how epithelial responses differ across age groups during viral infection.
elements_en.research_and_practice_implications: A deeper understanding of age-dependent epithelial responses is needed to uncover therapeutic targets for preventing and treating viral-associated respiratory failure. The review advocates for targeted research to address these gaps, particularly in elucidating the molecular and cellular pathways that contribute to severe outcomes in vulnerable age groups.

papers.title_zh: 呼吸道上皮 抗病毒药物 反应的年龄依赖性差异
papers.source_body_en: Age is an established risk factor for severe viral respiratory infections, yet the mechanisms driving increased severity of illness in infants and older adults remain incompletely understood. The respiratory epithelium is the primary target of viral infection and how it orchestrates the immune response may be a key determinant of clinical outcomes. The profound age-related difference in susceptibility to severe Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) brought increased attention to the epithelial response to viral infection in children and adults, adding significant data to the preexisting body of work largely focused on influenza and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). This review synthesizes current knowledge on the structural and functional differences in the respiratory epithelium between children and adults at baseline and during viral infection. We review the variable and heterogenous human studies in addition to in vitro and animal model data to identify key gaps in current knowledge. Here, we advocate for a more complete understanding of age-dependent differences in the respiratory epithelial response to viral infection to uncover therapeutic targets for prevention and treatment of viral-associated respiratory failure.

papers.title: Real-world effectiveness of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 vaccination in the prevention of RSV-related hospitalization among US adults aged ≥60 years.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: There is a growing body of evidence on the real-world effectiveness of adjuvanted respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) prefusion F3 (RSVPreF3) vaccination against RSV-related hospitalization among older adults. However, additional research is needed to further estimate vaccine effectiveness (VE) in subgroups at increased risk for severe RSV disease. RESEARCH QUESTION: What is the VE of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 vaccination against RSV-related hospitalization among adults aged ≥60 years in the United States (US), including subgroups at increased risk for severe RSV disease? STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort study utilized claims data from the Optum Research Database (ORD). Adjuvanted RSVPreF3-vaccinated and unvaccinated adults aged ≥60 years were identified (August 2023-May 2024) and exact matched 1:4 by age, sex, insurance type, and US state. Vaccination date was assigned as the index date. Baseline characteristics were measured during the 12-month pre-index period, with continuous enrollment required, and were balanced using propensity score-based weighting. Individuals were followed from 14 days post-index to the earliest of: disenrollment, death, RSV vaccination, or end of the analysis period (May 31, 2024). Hazard ratios (HRs) were estimated using Cox proportional hazards regression, comparing risk of RSV-related hospitalization, with VE calculated as (1 - HR) x 100%. RESULTS: The study included 520,440 vaccinated and 2,081,760 unvaccinated individuals. Median follow-up was 5.6 months, with a maximum of 9.7 months. Estimated VE was 75.6% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 69.8-80.2%). VE estimates in key subgroups included 72.5% (64.3-78.8%) among those with chronic pulmonary disease, 72.2% (64.1-78.4%) among those with cardiovascular disease, 82.3% (74.2-87.9%) among those with diabetes, and 71.4% (57.0-81.1%) among those who were immunocompromised. INTERPRETATION: These findings highlight the effectiveness of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 vaccination in preventing RSV-related hospitalization among older adults, including those at increased risk, suggesting that vaccination is an effective strategy in reducing RSV disease burden.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) causes severe disease in older adults, and while adjuvanted RSVPreF3 vaccination shows promise, prior evidence gaps remained regarding real-world effectiveness in preventing RSV-related hospitalization and in high-risk subgroups.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This retrospective cohort study used claims data from the Optum Research Database to compare adjuvanted RSVPreF3-vaccinated and unvaccinated adults aged 60 years or older in the United States between August 2023 and May 2024.
analysis.methods: Exact matching (1:4) by age, sex, insurance type, and US state was performed, with vaccination date as the index date. Baseline characteristics were measured during a 12-month pre-index period and balanced using propensity score-based weighting. Hazard ratios were estimated using Cox proportional hazards regression to calculate vaccine effectiveness (VE) as (1 - HR) x 100%.
analysis.main_results: The study included 520,440 vaccinated and 2,081,760 unvaccinated individuals with a median follow-up of 5.6 months. Overall VE against RSV-related hospitalization was 75.6% (95% CI: 69.8–80.2%). Subgroup VE estimates were 72.5% (64.3–78.8%) for chronic pulmonary disease, 72.2% (64.1–78.4%) for cardiovascular disease, 82.3% (74.2–87.9%) for diabetes, and 71.4% (57.0–81.1%) for immunocompromised individuals.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate that adjuvanted RSVPreF3 vaccination is effective in preventing RSV-related hospitalization in older adults, including those with chronic conditions or immunosuppression, addressing a key evidence gap in real-world effectiveness.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results support the use of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 vaccination as a strategy to reduce RSV disease burden and hospitalizations among adults aged 60 years and older, particularly in high-risk subgroups.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s retrospective design using claims data may introduce selection bias or unmeasured confounding, and follow-up was limited to a maximum of 9.7 months, which constrains the assessment of long-term effectiveness and safety.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective cohort study evaluated the real-world effectiveness of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 vaccination against RSV-related hospitalization among US adults aged 60 years or older using Optum Research Database claims data from August 2023 to May 2024. Exact matching and propensity score weighting balanced 520,440 vaccinated and 2,081,760 unvaccinated individuals. Vaccine effectiveness (VE) was 75.6% overall (95% CI: 69.8–80.2%) and ranged from 71.4% to 82.3% across subgroups with chronic pulmonary disease, cardiovascular disease, diabetes, or immunosuppression. The findings indicate that adjuvanted RSVPreF3 vaccination effectively reduces RSV-related hospitalizations in older adults, including high-risk groups, though limitations include potential bias from claims data and short follow-up duration.

papers.title_zh: 佐剂 RSVPreF3 疫苗接种 在预防 60 岁以上美国成年人中 RSV 相关住院治疗中的真实效果。
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: There is a growing body of evidence on the real-world effectiveness of adjuvanted respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) prefusion F3 (RSVPreF3) vaccination against RSV-related hospitalization among older adults. However, additional research is needed to further estimate vaccine effectiveness (VE) in subgroups at increased risk for severe RSV disease. RESEARCH QUESTION: What is the VE of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 vaccination against RSV-related hospitalization among adults aged ≥60 years in the United States (US), including subgroups at increased risk for severe RSV disease? STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort study utilized claims data from the Optum Research Database (ORD). Adjuvanted RSVPreF3-vaccinated and unvaccinated adults aged ≥60 years were identified (August 2023-May 2024) and exact matched 1:4 by age, sex, insurance type, and US state. Vaccination date was assigned as the index date. Baseline characteristics were measured during the 12-month pre-index period, with continuous enrollment required, and were balanced using propensity score-based weighting. Individuals were followed from 14 days post-index to the earliest of: disenrollment, death, RSV vaccination, or end of the analysis period (May 31, 2024). Hazard ratios (HRs) were estimated using Cox proportional hazards regression, comparing risk of RSV-related hospitalization, with VE calculated as (1 - HR) x 100%. RESULTS: The study included 520,440 vaccinated and 2,081,760 unvaccinated individuals. Median follow-up was 5.6 months, with a maximum of 9.7 months. Estimated VE was 75.6% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 69.8-80.2%). VE estimates in key subgroups included 72.5% (64.3-78.8%) among those with chronic pulmonary disease, 72.2% (64.1-78.4%) among those with cardiovascular disease, 82.3% (74.2-87.9%) among those with diabetes, and 71.4% (57.0-81.1%) among those who were immunocompromised. INTERPRETATION: These findings highlight the effectiveness of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 vaccination in preventing RSV-related hospitalization among older adults, including those at increased risk, suggesting that vaccination is an effective strategy in reducing RSV disease burden.

papers.title: Reactogenicity and Immunogenicity of Adjuvanted and Nonadjuvanted RSV Vaccines in Solid Organ Transplant Recipients
papers.abstract: Solid organ transplant (SOT) recipients are at high risk for severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). While RSV vaccine immunogenicity data in transplant populations are emerging, questions remain regarding the magnitude and durability of responses, cellular immunity, and determinants of decreased response. We conducted a prospective, single-center cohort study evaluating RSV vaccine reactogenicity and immunogenicity in SOT recipients compared with healthy controls. Serum was collected pre-vaccination and at 1, 3, and 6 mo post-vaccine to measure anti-fusion glycoprotein antibodies to RSV A and B and anti-nucleocapsid antibodies as a marker of natural infection. Peripheral blood mononuclear cells were collected from a subset for RSV-fusion (F)-specific cellular analyses. Forty-three SOT recipients (median age, 65) and 16 controls were enrolled (from October 2023 to January 2024). Mild reactogenicity occurred in ~25% of participants, with no severe events. In SOT recipients, anti-fusion glycoprotein IgG, RSV-F-specific CD4 + and CD8 + T cells increased significantly at 1 mo ( P < 0.01), with similar antibody fold changes to controls. Antibody responses remained durable through 6 mo; the rate of decline did not differ significantly between groups. Mycophenolate use was inversely correlated with antibody titers ( P < 0.05); vaccine type, organ, and time from transplant were not. The adjuvanted vaccine induced greater RSV-F-specific CD4 + T-cell responses at 3 mo. One SOT recipient developed RSV during the study. RSV vaccination was well tolerated and immunogenic in SOT recipients. Further research should optimize vaccination strategies and ideal timing for booster doses.

papers.title: In silico study: ADMET-driven pharmacokinetic profiling of antiviral compounds for pre-clinical screening framework of intranasal drug development.
papers.abstract: The ongoing emergence of respiratory viral pathogens, including novel variants and established threats such as influenza, severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), and Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV), continues to challenge global health systems due to limited specific therapeutic options. Intranasal antiviral delivery represents a promising approach for targeting respiratory tract infections; however, drug development frequently fails due to inappropriate pharmacokinetic properties. This study employed computational ADMET Predictor tools to systematically evaluate the physicochemical and potential pharmacokinetic properties of ten reference compounds, including nine approved antiviral drugs and ivermectin, a repurposed antiparasitic agent with reported antiviral activity and prior intranasal investigation: Zanamivir, Ribavirin, Oseltamivir, Favipiravir, Remdesivir, Nitazoxanide, Acyclovir, Lopinavir, Molnupiravir, and Ivermectin. Computational predictions were validated against experimental literature data to establish evidence-based criteria ranges. Key parameters related to intranasal drug delivery, covering physicochemical, absorption, distribution, metabolism, elimination, and toxicity properties, were systematically analyzed. The analysis resulted in revised criteria including molecular weight (Mwt), pH, lipophilicity (Log P), water solubility (Sw and SpH), Volume of distribution (Vd), P-glycoproteins substrate (Pgp substrate), and skin sensitization (Sens_Skin) to demonstrate 80% concordance with approved drug properties. This framework provides the preliminary evidence-based screening criteria as a tool to identify promising drug candidates suitable for preclinical evaluation in intranasal formulation development.
papers.journal: Journal of pharmacological and toxicological methods

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the unmet need for effective intranasal antiviral therapies amid the persistent threat of respiratory viruses such as influenza, SARS-CoV-2, and RSV, which lack sufficient specific treatments.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used a computational in silico design to evaluate ten reference compounds, including nine approved antivirals and ivermectin, for intranasal pharmacokinetic suitability.
analysis.methods: Computational ADMET Predictor tools were employed to systematically analyze physicochemical and pharmacokinetic properties, with predictions validated against experimental literature data to establish criteria ranges.
analysis.main_results: The analysis revised criteria including molecular weight, pH, lipophilicity, water solubility, volume of distribution, P-glycoprotein substrate status, and skin sensitization, achieving 80% concordance with approved drug properties.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the revised criteria as a preliminary evidence-based screening framework to identify promising intranasal drug candidates for preclinical evaluation, highlighting the novelty of applying ADMET-driven criteria specifically to intranasal antiviral development.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide a computational tool to streamline intranasal antiviral drug development, potentially accelerating the identification of candidates with favorable pharmacokinetic profiles for respiratory tract infections.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in silico predictions without experimental validation of pharmacokinetic behavior in intranasal formulations, which may reduce the reliability of the proposed criteria for direct clinical translation.

analysis.summary_en: This in silico study evaluated ten antiviral compounds, including approved drugs and ivermectin, using ADMET Predictor tools to assess their suitability for intranasal delivery. Systematic analysis of physicochemical and pharmacokinetic properties led to revised screening criteria with 80% concordance to approved drug properties. The authors propose this framework as a preliminary tool to identify promising candidates for preclinical intranasal antiviral development. However, the study relies solely on computational predictions without experimental validation, limiting the immediate applicability of the findings to clinical or preclinical settings.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究解决了在流感、SARS-CoV-2和RSV等呼吸道病毒持续威胁的情况下,对有效鼻内抗病毒药物疗法的未满足的需求,这些病毒缺乏足够的特异性治疗。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究采用计算机模拟设计来评估十种参考化合物,包括九种已批准的 抗病毒药物 和伊维菌素,以评估其鼻内药代动力学适用性。
elements_zh.methods: 采用计算 ADMET 预测器工具系统分析理化和药代动力学特性,并根据实验文献数据验证预测以确定标准范围。

papers.title_zh: 计算机模拟研究:ADMET 驱动的 抗病毒药物 化合物的药代动力学分析,用于鼻内药物开发的临床前筛选框架。
papers.source_body_en: The ongoing emergence of respiratory viral pathogens, including novel variants and established threats such as influenza, severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), and Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV), continues to challenge global health systems due to limited specific therapeutic options. Intranasal antiviral delivery represents a promising approach for targeting respiratory tract infections; however, drug development frequently fails due to inappropriate pharmacokinetic properties. This study employed computational ADMET Predictor tools to systematically evaluate the physicochemical and potential pharmacokinetic properties of ten reference compounds, including nine approved antiviral drugs and ivermectin, a repurposed antiparasitic agent with reported antiviral activity and prior intranasal investigation: Zanamivir, Ribavirin, Oseltamivir, Favipiravir, Remdesivir, Nitazoxanide, Acyclovir, Lopinavir, Molnupiravir, and Ivermectin. Computational predictions were validated against experimental literature data to establish evidence-based criteria ranges. Key parameters related to intranasal drug delivery, covering physicochemical, absorption, distribution, metabolism, elimination, and toxicity properties, were systematically analyzed. The analysis resulted in revised criteria including molecular weight (Mwt), pH, lipophilicity (Log P), water solubility (Sw and SpH), Volume of distribution (Vd), P-glycoproteins substrate (Pgp substrate), and skin sensitization (Sens_Skin) to demonstrate 80% concordance with approved drug properties. This framework provides the preliminary evidence-based screening criteria as a tool to identify promising drug candidates suitable for preclinical evaluation in intranasal formulation development.
papers.abstract_zh: 呼吸道病毒病原体的持续出现,包括流感、严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒 2 (SARS-CoV-2) 和 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 等新变种和既定威胁,由于具体治疗选择有限,继续对全球卫生系统构成挑战。鼻内 抗病毒药物 给药是一种治疗呼吸道感染的有前途的方法;然而,药物开发经常由于不适当的药代动力学特性而失败。本研究采用计算 ADMET Predictor 工具系统地评估了 10 种参考化合物的理化和潜在药代动力学特性,包括 9 种已批准的 抗病毒药物 药物和伊维菌素(一种重新利用的抗寄生虫药物,已报道 抗病毒药物 活性和先前的鼻内研究):扎那米韦、利巴韦林、奥司他韦、法匹拉韦、瑞德西韦、硝唑尼特、阿昔洛韦、洛匹那韦、莫努匹拉韦和伊维菌素。根据实验文献数据验证计算预测,以建立基于证据的标准范围。系统分析了与鼻内药物递送相关的关键参数,包括理化、吸收、分布、代谢、消除和毒性特性。分析结果修订了标准,包括分子量 (Mwt)、pH、亲脂性 (Log P)、水溶性(Sw 和 SpH)、分布体积 (Vd)、P-糖蛋白底物 (Pgp 底物) 和皮肤致敏性 (Sens_Skin),以证明与批准的药物特性 80% 的一致性。该框架提供了初步的循证筛选标准,作为识别适合鼻内制剂开发临床前评估的有前途的候选药物的工具。

papers.title: Immune Mechanisms Underlying Neonatal Protection Following Maternal RSV Vaccination
papers.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) remains a major cause of severe lower respiratory tract infection in early infancy, a period characterized by immunological immaturity and limited capacity for effective antiviral responses. Maternal RSV vaccination has emerged as a successful strategy to protect newborns by inducing high concentrations of IgG1-dominant, prefusion F-specific antibodies, which are selectively and actively transported across the placenta. This review synthesizes current mechanistic insights into how maternally derived antibodies confer neonatal protection, focusing on (i) FcRn-mediated transplacental transport, (ii) IgG subclass-specific differences in transfer and half-life, and (iii) the role of Fc glycosylation in modulating Fcγ receptor engagement and effector functions. Beyond neutralization, vaccine-induced antibodies mediate Fc-dependent mechanisms such as antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity and phagocytosis, which may be preferentially enriched in the neonatal circulation. Although emerging systems serology data suggest qualitative selectivity in placental transfer, evidence remains heterogeneous and highlights the need for further clarification of glycosylation-dependent and glycosylation-independent pathways. The timing of vaccination, maternal antibody characteristics, and placental integrity critically influence neonatal antibody levels and the duration of passive immunity. Understanding these molecular determinants is essential for optimizing maternal RSV immunization strategies and improving early-life protection.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in early infancy, focusing on maternal vaccination as an intervention to protect newborns through transplacental antibody transfer and neonatal immune mechanisms.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review synthesizes mechanistic insights on maternally derived antibodies conferring neonatal protection, including FcRn-mediated transplacental transport, IgG subclass-specific transfer, and Fc glycosylation effects, without reporting databases, search dates, or eligibility criteria.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Maternal RSV vaccination induces high concentrations of IgG1-dominant, prefusion F-specific antibodies that are actively transported across the placenta via FcRn, with Fc-dependent mechanisms such as antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity and phagocytosis potentially enriched in neonatal circulation.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Evidence on qualitative selectivity in placental transfer remains heterogeneous, particularly regarding glycosylation-dependent and glycosylation-independent pathways, and requires further clarification.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Optimizing maternal RSV immunization strategies requires attention to vaccination timing, maternal antibody characteristics, and placental integrity to enhance neonatal antibody levels and the duration of passive immunity.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores how maternal respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccination protects newborns by inducing IgG1-dominant, prefusion F-specific antibodies that are actively transported across the placenta via FcRn. The review highlights Fc-dependent mechanisms, such as antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity and phagocytosis, which may be enriched in neonatal circulation. However, evidence on the qualitative selectivity of placental transfer, particularly regarding Fc glycosylation pathways, remains heterogeneous and requires further clarification. Optimizing maternal immunization strategies depends on timing, maternal antibody characteristics, and placental integrity to maximize neonatal antibody levels and passive immunity duration.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述检查了婴儿早期的 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV),重点关注母体 呼吸道合胞病毒 作为通过胎盘抗体转移和新生儿免疫机制保护新生儿的干预措施。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述综合了有关赋予新生儿保护的母源抗体的机制见解,包括 FcRn 介导的经胎盘转运、IgG 亚类特异性转移和 Fc 糖基化效应,但没有报告数据库、搜索日期或资格标准。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 母体 RSV 疫苗接种 诱导高浓度的 IgG1 主导的融合前 F 特异性抗体,这些抗体通过 FcRn 主动转运穿过胎盘,具有 Fc 依赖性机制,例如抗体依赖性细胞毒性和吞噬作用,可能在新生儿循环中富集。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 关于胎盘转移的定性选择性的证据仍然存在异质性,特别是关于糖基化依赖性和糖基化非依赖性途径,需要进一步澄清。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 优化母体 RSV 免疫策略需要关注 疫苗接种 时机、母体抗体特征和胎盘完整性,以提高新生儿抗体水平和被动免疫持续时间。

papers.title: Dynamic regulation-based stabilizing mutations are highly effective for designing RSV pre-fusion F mRNA vaccines
papers.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of respiratory tract infections and poses a serious threat to young children, older adults, and immunocompromised individuals. We previously designed a pre-fusion stabilized F protein (pre-F), TriM-5, using a dynamic regulation mechanism, and produced a recombinant protein-based vaccine candidate that exhibited potent protection against RSV. However, several studies have revealed that the stabilization of pre-F achieved in protein form may not be sufficient for application in mRNA vaccine development. Here, based on TriM-5, we designed an mRNA vaccine candidate to assess whether the dynamic regulation-based stabilizing mutations of TriM-5 are also effective in an mRNA format. The TriM-5 mRNA was codon-optimized using in-house software named NVSI_GAmRNAopt, which employed a genetic algorithm incorporating multiple empirical parameters for coding sequence (CDS) optimization, and encapsulated using lipid nanoparticles (LNPs). Mouse immunization showed that after CDS optimization, the IgG antibody titers increased approximately threefold, indicating the effectiveness of our codon-optimization algorithm. Compared with the Moderna RSV mRNA sequence encapsulated with our proprietary BM028 LNPs, the TriM-5 mRNA-LNP induced 3.03-fold higher neutralizing antibody titers against RSV A2 virus, along with significantly higher IFN-γ, IL-5 and IL-17A secretion levels, indicating its superior immunogenicity. Virus challenge experiments demonstrated that both TriM-5 mRNA-LNP and Moderna mRNA-LNP reduced lung viral loads effectively, with no obvious lung pathology. The designed TriM-5 mRNA-LNP exhibits good immunogenicity and protective efficacy, and thereby may serve as a promising candidate for further vaccine development.
